370 implements the core/resident update bridge. An explicit PAL/NTSC update
on a full native base ensures an owned table exists, validates its pointer,
magic/version/size/record ID, then updates the current Point LONG. A failed
LONG restores the old bytes and does not commit host state. Foreign/malformed
tables reject updates. Original Point is never modified. Resident creation
can seed current Points from existing host state; originals remain boot values.
Portable MNTR publication reads the valid owned guest Point, so guest edits
are visible and a partial-axis core update retains the guest's other axis.

This file is the selectable work ledger for the Kickstart 3.1 graphics.library
replacement. It is intentionally separate from the design rationale and from
the execution evidence so an implementation pass can select one goal without
silently expanding into the other ownership domains.

The public ABI is the classic 68k layout: guest structures, vector offsets,
register conventions, signedness, and word alignment remain authoritative.
The portable implementation is the semantic reference. CopperStart exposes
that reference through checked register gateways, while a future native
CopperSharp68k ROM can replace the gateway bodies without changing the guest
layouts. CopperScreen owns host presentation and timing callbacks. CyberGraphX
and RTG surfaces are deliberately outside this ledger and retain their own
patch/provider boundary.

## Goal selection

Work should be selected by goal ID. A goal is complete only when its portable
contract, its applicable CopperStart/native gateway, direct-versus-mapped
coverage, and design/plan evidence are all updated. A goal may remain in
progress when provider-owned behavior is intentionally deferred; the deferred
boundary must be named rather than emulated implicitly.

| Goal | Unit | Portable contract | CopperSharp68k/CopperStart seam | CopperScreen seam |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G01 | ABI and guest layouts | V40 vector map, structure sizes, alignment, result signedness | Safe overlay and native tail-chain policy | none |
| G02 | Font lifecycle and selection | TextAttr/TextFont, Open/Close/Add/Rem/Extend/Strip, WeighTAMatch | Guest font-list and matcher gateway | optional font host projection |
| G03 | Text metrics | TextLength, TextExtent, TextFit, FontExtent | WORD/UWORD register inputs and classic result envelopes | none |
| G04 | RastPort text | glyph decode, JAM modes, styles, cursor boundary | Text/SetFont gateway | layer clipping/damage provider only |
| G05 | RastPort state and styles | pens, draw mode, masks, soft styles, RP attributes | checked tag-list gateway | layer state provider only |
| G06 | Pixels and lines | Read/WritePixel, Move, Draw, PolyDraw, patterns | direct and mapped planar path | layer clipping provider only |
| G07 | Rectangles and scrolling | fills, clears, EraseRect, ScrollRaster/BF | transactional planar operations | layer damage/backing-store provider only |
| G08 | Areas and flood | AreaInfo/TmpRas, AreaEnd, ellipse, Flood | collector and fill gateway | layer clipping provider only |
| G09 | Bitmap lifecycle | Init/Alloc/FreeBitMap, Alloc/FreeRaster, attributes | ownership, alignment, and optional display-DMA address-class boundary | display-DMA callback only |

| G11 | Templates and patterns | BltTemplate, BltPattern, masked blits, BltClear | guest buffer validation and ABI results | layer provider boundary |
| G12 | Blitter ownership | Own/Disown/Wait/QBlit/QBSBlit | scheduler/custom-chip status callbacks | beam timing owner |
| G13 | Regions and copper helpers | regions, user copper construction and teardown | bounded guest ownership | custom-chip publication only |
| G14 | Palette and pens | ColorMap, RGB4/RGB32, Obtain/Release/FindColor, VideoControl | transactional palette/tag boundary | copper palette publication |
| G15 | View/ViewPort lifecycle | InitView/InitVPort, MakeVPort, MrgCop, LoadView, Free* | exact RasInfo cardinality and active-view publication | frame-boundary/copper handoff |

## Implementation order

The first delivery slice is G04, G06, and G15, with G18 providing the
screen-facing lifecycle integration. G02 and G03 supply the font and metric
contracts consumed by G04. G05 and G07 provide the RastPort state and fill
semantics consumed by G06. G24 is a boundary goal, not permission to move
layer clipping into graphics.library. G26 is a later implementation option;
all portable units must keep their guest layout and provider contracts stable
so a native 68k body can be substituted independently.

  earlier links and D0 untouched for the provider boundary.

- G15/G18 screen-resource close ownership: an explicit `CloseScreen` now
  retains a committed optional graphics resource handoff when synthetic
  teardown declines (for example, while public screen links are still owned
  elsewhere). Prepared resources are tracked by their exact Screen, so a
  successful foreign close cannot retire them; a successful owning close does
  so exactly once—even if the host receives a repeated successful close.
  Failed opens retain their existing request-scoped rollback finalization.

- G24/G25 projected-layer rollback: a successful provider-owned `SetRast`
  followed by a deliberately failed projected `ClipBlit` leaves the Layer's
  public flags and the complete `DamageList` header unchanged. Graphics restores
  its visible/public, backing-store, and SuperBitMap writes transactionally;
  only layers.library may publish refresh or damage topology.

- G24 suspended refresh clipping: after a caller ends an update with
  `complete=FALSE`, it may replace the caller-owned ClipRegion before the
  retained damage is refreshed. The following `BeginUpdate` intersects the
  Layers-owned damage with every Region rectangle, including disjoint islands;
  graphics paints only that temporary projection and cannot consume or mutate
  DamageList. A successful outer `EndUpdate(TRUE)` is the sole operation that
  retires the retained damage and refresh state. If the private damage-block
  release is rejected, both public and private ownership remain published for
  a safe retry rather than leaking a forgotten allocation.

- G15/G18 display database: `NextDisplayInfo` returns public ModeID keys,
  including the valid zero default-lores key; `FindDisplayInfo` alone uses
  the private nonzero compatibility handle. `GetDisplayInfoData` publishes
  `QueryHeader.Length` in 8-byte double-longword units for all four portable
  `DTAG_*` chunks.
- G15/G18 mapped enumeration: direct and register-gateway iteration now agree
  from `INVALID_ID` through all 66 native OCS/ECS records and the terminating
  `INVALID_ID`; the private default-mode compatibility handle advances only
  as an input courtesy and is never published as a public mode key.
- G15/G18 capability flow: `ModeNotAvailable` propagates the active OCS/ECS
  capability through record resolution; direct and mapped OCS-only queries
  keep SuperHires enumerable but report `DI_AVAIL_NO_CHIPS`.
- G02/G04/G06: matcher field access, direct planar `WritePixel` minterms, and
  the initial text/drawing/lifecycle gateway slices are recorded in the
  execution plan; layer clipping/damage and native custom-chip timing remain
  explicit provider gates.
- G05/G06: `SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, and `SetDrMd` now preflight their complete
  multi-field RastPort publication (requested byte, derived minterms,
  line-pattern phase, and Flags) before mutation. Direct and mapped late-write
  regressions preserve the full guest state and D0 on provider decline;
  CyberGraphX remains outside this boundary.
- G07: `SetRast` now accepts a selected plane span whose inclusive final byte
  is `$FFFFFFFF`, matching the 32-bit guest address envelope already used by
  the other planar primitives. Direct and mapped coverage proves the full
  two-plane initialization and preserves the void-vector register contract;
  wrapped spans remain available to native/provider ownership.
- G16/G17: status-aware `VBeamPos` now declines a display backend that lacks a
  cycle-accurate beam callback instead of claiming the legacy zero result.
  Direct callback and mapped timing paths remain unchanged; the untimed
  compatibility accessor stays explicit and separate.
- G15/G18: synthetic `ScreenToFront` now has an optional state-aware activation
  seam that re-enters `LoadView` without mutating the caller's register frame
  and preserves any scheduler cycle advance. Direct lifecycle coverage proves
  the mutable-frame result; the CopperStart screen gateway covers mapped
  handoff. Legacy cycle-only hosts remain supported.
- G15/G18: a declined state-aware `ScreenToFront` activation now remains
  unclaimed instead of falling through to the legacy viewport selector. This
  keeps foreign/provider-owned screens available to their owner and preserves
the caller frame on decline; direct lifecycle coverage passes.
- G03: zero-length `TextFit` now publishes its empty `TextExtent` before
  decoding `rp->Font`, matching the classic no-render path and preserving
  provider ownership for a foreign or unreadable selected font. Direct and
  mapped overlay coverage passes; non-empty metric calls retain full font and
  guest-span validation.
- G08: `Flood` now rejects an aggregate logical-cell workload whose required
  destination preflight, rollback snapshot, and connected-region traversal
  would exceed the portable host work contract. The decline occurs before
  TmpRas, seed, pattern, plane, or destination staging; direct, register, and
  mapped ROM-overlay coverage preserve D0, cycles, and native ownership.
- G10: `BltBitMap` and `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` now reject representable
  rectangles whose staged source/destination/mask pixels, rollback snapshot,
  and publication would exceed the portable host work contract before TempA,
  external-mask, scratch, or plane-pointer probing. Direct, register, and
  native-overlay coverage preserve D0/cycles and keep malformed/provider
  endpoints available to their owner.
- G19: `BitMapScale` now rejects a destination rectangle whose three logical
  sample/probe, rollback-snapshot, and publication passes would exceed the
  portable host work contract before allocating DDA/sample staging. Direct
  and CopperStart coverage preserves destination extents and planar bytes;
  native-overlay calls with caller-owned endpoints remain unclaimed for the
  resident/provider owner.
- G09/G19: `BMF_INTERLEAVED` now uses the Kickstart row-interleaved layout
  end-to-end. `AllocBitMap`, `FreeBitMap`, display-envelope admission,
  planar blits, drawing/snapshots, and `BitMapScale` derive the aggregate
  row stride while retaining per-plane widths and contiguous ownership;
  ECS/AGA allocation fails when that contiguous block is unavailable, while
  OCS ignores the flag as documented. Direct/register interleaved scaling and
  full graphics-scaffold coverage pass.
- G14: `GetRGB4` now has a requested-field ownership boundary: after the
  instance-owned map/count check it reads only the selected `ColorTable`
  word. `ColorMap.Type` and the optional `LowColorBits` extension are not
  consumed by this legacy 12-bit result, so sparse provider-owned extension
  storage cannot steal a valid query. Pure and CopperStart direct coverage
  pass; RGB32 and palette mutation retain their complete-entry transactions.
- G18: synthetic `OpenScreen` now publishes an owned default `ColorMap` for
  every standard-planar viewport, not only requests carrying palette or
  `VideoControl` tags. The map uses the classic `max(32, 1<<depth)` default;
  close clears its owned header before returning the Exec block so a later
  un-cleared `AllocMem` request cannot inherit stale map fields. OpenScreen
  lifecycle and broader boot-memory coverage pass; CyberGraphX/RTG screens
  remain outside this standard-planar path.
- G06: zero-length `PolyDraw` now claims the classic low-UWORD no-op before
  reading the RastPort or point table. Direct and mapped overlay coverage
  preserves D0/cycles for unreadable/provider-owned endpoints; nonzero streams
  retain complete point and destination preflight.
- G02/G04: `CloseFont(NULL)` now remains a safe ABI no-op even on a native
  overlay that has no rebound guest TextFonts list. Non-null font handles
  still require the explicit lifecycle backend and remain available to
  Kickstart/provider ownership; direct and mapped coverage preserve D0,
  cycles, and the native return frame.
- G02/G04: `StripFont(NULL)` now follows the same safe no-op boundary. Native
  overlays may claim the null form without a guest font-list backend, while
  non-null extension detachment remains owned by the selected lifecycle
  provider; direct and mapped coverage preserve D0, cycles, and return state.
- G02/G04: the shared portable `StripFont` body now also claims the null
  teardown form, keeping direct CopperSharp68k-compatible calls aligned with
  the register gateway while non-null extension ownership remains provider-
  checked.
- G06: `RectFill` now treats inverted guest bounds as the documented empty
  void operation. The portable core returns success without probing or
  mutating the bitmap, and direct plus mapped native-overlay calls preserve
  D0/cycles and the prior pixels. Malformed RastPorts and layer/provider
  ownership remain separate failure boundaries.
- G07: `ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` now apply the same empty-rectangle
  rule to reversed bounds. Both void vectors return success without touching
  bitmap or line state, with pure, direct, mapped, and malformed-row-stride
  coverage; non-inverted geometry retains the existing clipping and backfill
  behavior.
- G07: non-layered `EraseRect` now follows the same inverted-bound no-op as
  its underlying `RectFill` path. Pure and direct/mapped overlay calls leave
  the prior planar pixels and line state unchanged; layered erase remains a
  provider boundary.
- G06/G07: the empty-geometry fast paths now validate the RastPort layer
  owner before claiming `RectFill`, `BltPattern`, `ScrollRaster`,
  `ScrollRasterBF`, or `EraseRect`. Pure calls on layered RastPorts still
  decline without a visibility predicate, while provider-backed calls retain

- G15/G16: `FreeVPortCopLists` now claims an already-empty public copper-link
  envelope as a successful teardown no-op even when no display resource owner

- G15/G18: synthetic `ScreenToFront` now treats an already-front owned screen
  as a successful idempotent no-op. It checks the host current-View cache and,

  duplicate frame-boundary copper request; a foreign mapped `ActiView` keeps
  the screen eligible for an explicit takeover. Boot-level coverage verifies
  both the no-requeue and provider/native-replacement paths.
- G15/G18: the boot-side `LoadView` path now applies the same bounded
  View/ViewPort/RasInfo/BitMap topology fingerprint as the portable core.
  Repeating an unchanged active View repairs `GfxBase->ActiView` without
  queueing a second frame handoff, while edited ViewPort geometry invalidates
  the fingerprint and schedules a fresh publication. `ScreenToFront` keeps
  its explicit takeover path by invalidating the fingerprint before reclaiming
  a View whose guest active-view sidecar was replaced. Direct portable and
  mapped boot coverage exercise both branches; CyberGraphX remains outside
  this standard-planar lifecycle boundary.
- G15/G18: boot-side `LoadView(NULL)` now uses the same idempotent blank-stream
  rule. Once the display is already blank and the guest `GfxBase->ActiView`
  still agrees, a repeated NULL request repairs only the sidecar and does not
  queue another frame-boundary blanking handoff. A directly replaced guest
  active-view pointer remains eligible for the normal reclaim path; mapped
  lifecycle coverage exercises both states.
- G15/G18: successful synthetic `CloseScreen` now invalidates the boot-side
  published View topology fingerprint even when a foreign View remains active,
  preventing stale teardown metadata from affecting a later session; close/open
  regression coverage verifies the cache is retired.
- G01/G04/G06/G07: the shared RastPort field envelope now rejects address zero
  before probing host memory. Text and drawing vectors therefore preserve the
  native/provider handoff for a mapped NULL RastPort, with direct and ROM-overlay
  coverage proving unchanged D0 and cycles for Text, Draw, ReadPixel, and
  WritePixel.
- G06: connected `PolyDraw` now bounds the aggregate Bresenham walk across
  the complete UWORD point stream before probing or publishing any planar
  destination. A maximal stream of signed-WORD endpoints therefore declines
  instead of entering a multi-billion-sample host traversal; the existing
  zero-mask state-only path and ordinary connected-line phase remain intact.
- G01/G06: pen and draw-mode setters now enter that same RastPort ownership
  guard before their first old-value read. Odd or NULL bases therefore cannot
  be observed through a host byte-addressable mapping, and the focused direct
  regression verifies zero host probes for both rejected forms.
- G01/G06: non-empty `PolyDraw` now rejects NULL and odd point-table bases
  before reading coordinate words. Direct and ROM-overlay coverage preserves
  the native/provider handoff, while the documented low-UWORD zero-count
  no-op remains claimable.
- G01/G06: V36 pixel-array status adapters now validate an explicit temporary
  RastPort only after the portable operation would reach that workspace. Odd
  or malformed temporary structures therefore decline to the resident/
  provider owner without changing ordinary geometry, source-array, or
  zero-mask `-1`/success results. Direct coverage spans all four line/array
  status vectors, and the mapped overlay gate proves D0/cycle/planar parity.

## G06/G19 pixel-array aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

V36/V40 pixel-array conversion now rejects aggregate logical-pixel and
padded-array work beyond the portable `Int32.MaxValue` host envelope before
array staging, planar snapshots, or publication. Structurally unrepresentable
guest envelopes retain the classic claimed `-1` result; valid oversized work
remains available to native/provider ownership. Pure, CopperStart, and mapped
overlay coverage preserves D0/cycles and avoids a multi-billion-byte host walk.

## G08 AreaEnd aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`AreaEnd` now bounds the aggregate logical-cell work of decoded polygons and
ellipses before acquiring managed masks, guest `TmpRas` scratch, destination
plane snapshots, or fill publication. A representable but multi-billion-cell
shape therefore remains available to native/provider ownership without
partially consuming the collector or touching planar storage. Empty streams,
zero effective masks, inverse-JAM1 no-ops, and structurally malformed inputs
retain their existing result and ownership contracts.

## G10 BltBitMap aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltBitMap` and `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` now bound their logical-cell work for
source/destination (and external-mask) staging, rollback snapshot, and
publication before overlap/TempA or external-mask checks, reusable scratch
growth, or plane-pointer reads. A full signed-WORD rectangle can be
structurally valid while still requiring a multi-billion-entry host
traversal; that request declines without guest-raster or allocator side
effects. Small standard-planar copies, overlap handling, and the separate
CyberGraphX/layer provider boundaries retain their existing contracts.

## G11 BltTemplate aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltTemplate` now bounds the clipped template decode, destination rollback,
and publication work before reading the template source or growing reusable
scratch. A representable full signed-WORD rectangle therefore declines before
host allocation or guest-raster probing, while the existing zero-mask no-op,
template alignment, draw-mode, and layer/provider semantics remain unchanged.

## G07 ScrollRaster aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` now reject a representable destination
whose source staging, destination preflight, rollback snapshot, and
publication would exceed the portable `Int32.MaxValue` host-work envelope.
The guard runs after the full-displacement no-op boundary but before source
plane or line-state reads, preserving native/provider ownership without a
large host walk. Pure and direct-vs-mapped overlay coverage preserve D0,
cycles, and the prior guest raster; ordinary clipped overlap and BPen
backfill behavior remain unchanged.

## G07 ClearScreen aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`ClearScreen` now admits its complete text-prefix and remaining-row
transaction as one bounded unit. The four probe/publication passes and the
selected-plane rollback bytes are accounted for before line-state or plane
storage reads, so two individually representable spans cannot combine into an
unbounded host walk. A zero-mask clear retains its successful line-pattern
update; direct and ROM-overlay coverage preserve D0/cycles and the existing
standard-planar/provider ownership split.

## G11 BltClear aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltClear` now admits its complete byte-span transaction as three bounded
passes: destination probe, rollback snapshot, and fill publication. A
guest-valid span that exceeds the portable host-work envelope declines before
the first destination read or managed allocation, preserving the classic D0,
cycles, and native/provider boundary. Word alignment, rows-mode, fill-word,
and late-write rollback semantics remain unchanged.

## G07/G11 BltPattern aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`BltPattern` now bounds the complete full-raster pattern transaction: pattern
or stencil evaluation, destination preflight, rollback snapshot, and
publication. The admission check runs before external-stencil or plane reads
and preserves the successful zero-mask and inverse-JAM1 no-op paths. Direct
and ROM-overlay decline coverage keeps D0/cycles and native/provider ownership
unchanged.

## G04 Text selected-plane aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`Text` now includes the effective selected-plane count in its bounded
background, underline, glyph-cell, bold-smear, rollback, and publication work
admission. A representable multi-plane text cell whose rollback journal would
exceed the portable `Int32.MaxValue` host envelope declines before destination
preflight, preserving the cursor and native/provider handoff. Pure and
direct-vs-ROM-overlay coverage preserve D0/cycles; zero-mask cursor behavior,
glyph decoding, Layers, and CyberGraphX ownership remain separate.

## G07 SetRast selected-plane aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`SetRast` now admits its probe, rollback, and publication transaction using
the effective selected-plane count. A representable deep bitmap can therefore
decline before plane-pointer reads when the complete host work envelope would
be exceeded, while zero-mask, ordinary single-plane, and visibility-aware
provider behavior remain intact. Pure and direct-vs-ROM-overlay coverage
preserve D0/cycles and native/provider ownership.

## G07 ClearEOL selected-plane aggregate-work ownership (2026-08-13)

`ClearEOL` now admits its outer rollback plus nested fill transaction using
the effective selected-plane count before destination staging. A representable
deep bitmap therefore declines before plane reads when the complete host work
envelope would be exceeded, while zero-mask, line-phase, and layer-provider
semantics remain intact. Pure and direct-vs-ROM-overlay coverage preserve the
void-vector D0/cycle frame.

## G07 EraseRect combined-transaction ownership (2026-08-13)

`EraseRect` now admits its outer rollback plus delegated `RectFill`/`BltPattern`
work using selected-plane depth before minterm or destination staging. A
representable large rectangle therefore declines before guest raster reads
when the complete host envelope would be exceeded, preserving the void D0/cycle
frame and layer-provider ownership. Inverted and zero-mask semantics remain
intact; pure and direct-vs-ROM-overlay coverage exercise the boundary.

## G06/G07 DrawEllipse bounding-transaction ownership (2026-08-13)

`DrawEllipse` now admits its full bounding-box rollback snapshot together with
selected-plane outline probing and publication before destination storage is
read. A representable maximum ellipse therefore declines before an
unbounded host walk or plane probe, while zero-mask, non-layered clipping, and
layer-provider semantics remain intact. Pure and direct-vs-ROM-overlay
coverage preserve the void D0/cycle frame.

## G02/G04 InitRastPort default-font ownership (2026-08-13)

When the compatibility default-font provider returns a nonzero guest
`TextFont`, `InitRastPort` now requires the complete font to decode before it
claims the void vector. An undecodable default remains available to native
Kickstart or another provider instead of producing a fontless success;
successful default metrics and late-write rollback retain their existing
behavior. Direct register coverage verifies D0, cycles, and the complete
RastPort envelope remain unchanged on this decline.

## G03 TextFit explicit vertical-constraint ownership (2026-08-13)

When `TextFit` receives an explicit `TextExtent`, the portable metric path now
checks the constraint's Y bounds and height against the selected font before
walking the string. An impossible vertical envelope publishes the empty
extent successfully, even if a later character is malformed or unavailable,
matching the native short-circuit and keeping provider-owned glyph storage
from changing the result. Horizontal prefix fitting and the alternate
width/height form remain separate checks.

## G03 FontExtent default-glyph boundary (2026-08-13)

`FontExtent` now includes the optional trailing default glyph stored after the
declared `TextFont.LoChar..HiChar` range whenever the selected font backend can
decode that guest table entry. This keeps the maximum width and horizontal
envelope compatible with native TextFont fallback behavior without requiring
lightweight host providers to invent an index-based accessor.
The guest-memory implementation reads the slot directly by table index, so a
full `0..255` declared range is covered as well.

## G06/G07 RectFill no-pattern field ownership (2026-08-13)

The no-area-pattern `RectFill` path now claims only the RastPort fields used by
that native fast path. `AreaPtSz` is decoded only when `AreaPtrn` is non-null,
so a malformed or provider-owned trailing pattern-size byte cannot steal an
otherwise valid solid fill. Patterned `RectFill`/`BltPattern` calls retain the
full signed pattern-height validation, and pure plus CopperStart coverage
preserve the void-vector register boundary.

## G08 AreaEnd no-pattern field ownership (2026-08-14)

`AreaEnd` now decodes `AreaPtSz` only when `AreaPtrn` is non-null. A valid
no-pattern area fill therefore remains claimable when the trailing pattern
size byte is unavailable, while patterned area fills retain strict signed
pattern-height validation. Pure and CopperStart coverage preserve the
collector reset and void/status ABI.

## G08 Flood no-pattern field ownership (2026-08-14)

`Flood` now decodes `AreaPtSz` only when `AreaPtrn` is non-null. A valid
no-pattern seed-color flood therefore remains claimable when the trailing
pattern-size byte is unavailable, while patterned floods retain strict signed
pattern-height validation. Pure and CopperStart coverage preserve connected
region mutation and the void/status ABI.

## G14 FreeColorMap NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeColorMap(NULL)` now claims the documented successful void no-op without
allocator or palette-lock work. Non-null foreign, stale, and malformed maps
remain unclaimed, preserving native/provider and CyberGraphX ownership. Pure,
register, and mapped-overlay coverage preserve D0 and cycles.

## G16 FreeCopList NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeCopList(NULL)` now claims the successful empty-list teardown without
allocator or registry work. Non-null foreign and stale lists remain unclaimed
for native/provider ownership. Pure, register, and direct-vs-mapped overlay
coverage preserve D0 and cycles.

## G16 FreeCprList NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeCprList(NULL)` now claims the successful empty-list teardown without
public-envelope, allocator, or optional-backend work. Non-null foreign, stale,
and malformed lists remain unclaimed for native/provider ownership. Pure,
register, and direct-vs-mapped overlay coverage preserve D0 and cycles.

## G09/G19 FreeBitMap NULL-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`FreeBitMap(NULL)` now claims the successful empty-list teardown without
registry, allocator, or guest-header work. Non-null foreign, stale, and
malformed standard bitmaps remain unclaimed; RTG/provider-owned forms retain
their separate boundary. Pure, register, and mapped-overlay coverage preserve
D0, cycles, and allocator state.

## G22/G25 GfxFree metadata ownership (2026-08-14)

`GfxFree` now claims only an instance-owned node whose guest metadata still
identifies the graphics subsystem and its allocated subtype. Corrupted
metadata remains unclaimed for native/provider ownership; direct, register,
and mapped overlay coverage preserves D0, cycles, association, and allocator
state.

## G02/G03 WeighTAMatch zero-size metric input (2026-08-14)

`WeighTAMatch` now accepts a readable `TextAttr` with `ta_YSize == 0` and
returns the native exact metric when the remaining scored fields match.
`OpenFont` retains its separate nonzero selected-font envelope validation;
direct, register, and mapped coverage prove the metric result and malformed
odd-address handoff.

## G02/G03 WeighTAMatch signed-penalty width (2026-08-14)

The asymmetric size penalty now wraps through the native signed `WORD`
temporary before comparison and subtraction. Upward deltas in the 256..511
range therefore retain Kickstart's wrapped positive/negative metric behavior;
pure, register, and mapped coverage prove the exact result and ABI state.

## G02/G03 OpenFont zero-size request (2026-08-14)

`OpenFont` now carries a readable zero-size request into resident-font
matching. Valid candidates still require a nonzero, readable `TextFont`
strike and lifecycle envelope; direct/register and rebound-list mapped
coverage prove successful open/close behavior and preserve malformed fallback.

## G02/G04 CloseFont resident-list ownership (2026-08-14)

Final close now removes non-ROM fonts opened from a rebound guest font list,
while no-remove extensions remain public and malformed list state stays
native/provider-owned. Direct/register and mapped coverage prove accessor,
list-link, D0, and cycle behavior.

### G18 Display query sentinel ownership (2026-08-14)

The portable display-query boundary now claims the universal `INVALID_ID`
sentinel: `FindDisplayInfo` returns NULL, `ModeNotAvailable` returns
`DI_AVAIL_NOMONITOR`, and null-handle `GetDisplayInfoData` returns zero without
touching the guest buffer. Unknown non-sentinel mode IDs remain available to
native monitor/CyberGraphX providers. Pure, register, and mapped-overlay
coverage is complete; full display-database timing and provider parity remain
open.

### G14 `ReleasePen(-1)` sentinel ownership (2026-08-14)

The all-ones `ReleasePen` argument is a successful no-op that does not inspect
the ColorMap. The portable register boundary now claims it before ownership
checks, with direct and mapped overlay coverage proving D0/cycle parity for a
foreign or unmapped A0. Non-sentinel releases remain strict; the graphics
scaffold is green at 995/995. Palette timing and CyberGraphX remain separate
gates.

## G15/G26/G27 Odd native GfxBase sidecar ownership (2026-08-14)

The optional native `GfxBase->ActiView` sidecar now requires an even discovered
graphics-library base. A byte-readable odd base declines before the portable
path probes or writes its LONG fields, and an odd rebind leaves the existing
portable registry base intact. Direct and native-overlay dispatch coverage
preserves D0/cycles, display callbacks, and the guest active-view pointer;
aligned native bases retain the normal LoadView publication order.

The reversible CopperStart ROM-overlay installer applies the same boundary:
odd native graphics.library bases are rejected before mapped vector probing or
host-gateway replacement, preserving the resident image for native/provider
ownership.

The CopperScreen/AmigaBoot lifecycle bridge applies the same boundary when it
reconciles `ActiView` or publishes `ChipRevBits0`: odd discovered native bases
are never read or written through the host byte adapter, so blanking and
`ScreenToFront` remain available to native/provider ownership.

## G15/G17 Host View-chain alignment ownership (2026-08-14)

The AmigaBoot bridge's shared WORD/LONG readers now reject odd guest
addresses. An odd `View` base and an odd linked `ViewPort` are left for the
native/provider implementation before copper resolution or `ActiView`
publication; byte-packed fields retain their byte-reader path. Focused boot
coverage verifies unchanged D0/cycles, caller pointers, and the prior active
view sidecar.

## G06 Connected COMPLEMENT/JAM2 zero-pattern ownership (2026-08-14)

Connected `Draw` segments now undo their shared endpoint for every actual
`COMPLEMENT` sample, including `JAM2` pattern-zero samples that use `BPen`.
The line preflight predicate matches the publication predicate, preserving
transactional rollback. Direct planar coverage exercises the phase transition;
exact ROM timing and layered/provider damage remain open.

## G07 Zero-mask scroll line-state ownership (2026-08-14)

A real `ScrollRaster` or `ScrollRasterBF` displacement restarts `linpatcnt`
at 15 even when the effective write mask selects no planes, but it does not
stage source pixels or mutate the bitmap. Zero displacement remains a no-op,
and a failed phase publication remains transactional. Direct planar coverage
exercises both scroll variants; full layer damage and ROM timing remain open.

## Completion rule

Do not mark the replacement complete because every vector has a switch case.
Completion requires: (1) all selected semantic goals have direct and mapped
coverage, (2) malformed input preserves the native/provider handoff, (3)
screen/view publication is ordered at the documented frame/timing boundary,
(4) CyberGraphX remains a separate patch, and (5) the execution plan records
the remaining provider/native gates and their evidence.

See [`GRAPHICS_LIBRARY_REPLACEMENT_DESIGN.md`](GRAPHICS_LIBRARY_REPLACEMENT_DESIGN.md)
for rationale and [`GRAPHICS_LIBRARY_REPLACEMENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md`](GRAPHICS_LIBRARY_REPLACEMENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md)
for implementation evidence.
## G04 Fixed-cell unsigned advance ownership (2026-08-14)

The decoded fixed-cell text path now accepts the complete unsigned `tf_XSize`
WORD range when `tf_CharSpace` is absent, including the negative
`FPF_REVPATH` representation. Text rendering, destination/work preflight,
underline calculation, and metric accumulation use the same `-65535..65535`
movement boundary; explicit `CharSpace` tables retain signed-WORD validation.
The UWORD `TextExtent.te_Width` field preserves the wrapped 16-bit form for
reverse-path results below `-32768`. A focused planar/metric regression covers
a 40000-pixel cell and the signed public cursor clamp. Provider clipping,
exact ROM timing, and CyberGraphX remain open.

## G17 All-hidden viewport rethink ownership (2026-08-14)

`RethinkDisplay` validates an all-hidden `ViewPort` chain but leaves the
currently published CPR/raw copper stream and active-view sidecar untouched.
Focused AmigaBoot coverage proves the no-op publication boundary and keeps
later visible viewport rebuilding available; scheduler timing and provider
damage remain separate gates.

Malformed viewport reconstruction and copper-publication failure now return
the documented nonzero V39+ `RethinkDisplay` status, while the valid all-hidden
case returns zero and preserves the active stream. Exact ROM version gating,
frame timing, and provider damage remain separate gates.

## G19 Layer-provider UWORD pixel arrays (2026-08-14)

Layered V36 pixel-line and pixel-array callbacks now retain their documented
UWORD coordinates, widths, and endpoints through the register adapter and
Layers bridge. Values above 32767 no longer become negative provider inputs;
the high-coordinate forwarding regression keeps this provider contract aligned
with the standard planar path. Layer clipping/damage and RTG ownership remain
separate provider gates.

## G02/G15 Screen-font residency (2026-08-14)

The reset-scoped compatibility default font is treated as resident across
screen teardown/reopen. Closing the last screen-owned accessor clears the
accessor count without setting `FPF_REMOVED`, while ordinary non-ROM fonts
continue to follow the last-close removal rule. Direct font-backend coverage
and an AmigaBoot two-screen lifecycle regression verify the guest font pointer,
accessor count, and reopen behavior. Native font-list weighting and provider
font ownership remain separate goals.

## G04 ColorTextFont planar composition (2026-08-14)

The memory-backed planar `Text` path now decodes the V40 `ColorTextFont`
extension when `FSF_COLORFONT` is set. It validates the bounded source-plane
strike envelope, composes source bits through the guest `PlanePick` and
`PlaneOnOff` mapping, honors the dynamic `FgColor` remap, and applies the
resulting color index through the RastPort write mask and draw mode. Metrics,
cursor movement, styles, rollback, and line-state publication stay shared
with ordinary TextFont rendering. Backends that do not expose the classic
color-font extension still decline before mutation, leaving native/provider
ownership intact; full color-table/RTG palette mapping and CyberGraphX remain
separate gates.

## G02/G03 Tagged WeighTAMatch request-envelope ownership (2026-08-14)

The pure `WeighTAMatch` path now validates a tagged request's `tta_Tags`
suffix whenever `FSF_TAGGED` is set, even when the target font supplies no tag
list through A2. A malformed `TAG_MORE` continuation therefore declines
before publishing a zero or positive score instead of silently becoming an
untagged match. Direct, register, and native-overlay coverage preserve D0,
cycles, and the native tail-chain on malformed input; ordinary untagged
requests still do not dereference a tag suffix.

## Validation snapshot (2026-08-14)

The normal emulator/test project-reference build completes with zero
warnings/errors. The complete `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` filter
passes 1017/1017. This is evidence for the implemented units only; it does not
close the remaining native CopperSharp68k, exact-ROM timing, layer

provider, RTG, and CyberGraphX goals.

## G15/G18 OpenScreen display-reconstruction atomicity (2026-08-14)

The CopperStart Intuition bridge now treats a nonzero `RethinkDisplay`
reconstruction status as an `OpenScreen` failure. Both legacy and tag-list
screen opens invoke the existing `CloseScreen` ownership path for the newly
allocated guest Screen before returning `NULL`, so a failed viewport/copper
publication cannot leak a half-open Screen into a later retry. Focused host
lifecycle tests cover both entry points; exact Kickstart failure codes and
provider-specific display rollback remain separate gates.

## G15/G18 OpenScreen error-code finalization (2026-08-14)

The synthetic bridge now keeps the request-scoped `SA_ErrorCode` destination
through the final display handoff. Construction leaves the destination
unpublished until `OpenScreen`/`OpenScreenTagList` finalize it after
`RethinkDisplay` succeeds; a failed reconstruction rolls the Screen back first
and then publishes the staged allocation error. The new context callback keeps
this finalization optional for CopperScreen/native hosts, while preserving
foreign/provider ownership and the existing exact-screen rollback boundary.

## G09 layers/bitmap null-handle ownership (2026-08-14)

`SyncSBitMap` and `CopySBitMap` now reject a null Layer handle before invoking
an optional layers/native callback. Direct and register coverage preserves the
caller D0/cycle state on the declined malformed call, and the host callback
coverage proves that neither provider sees the null address. Non-null Layer
handles remain an explicit provider boundary; private SuperBitMap and ClipRect
copying, clipping, and damage remain outside the portable graphics slice.

## G19 BitMapScale source-plane ownership (2026-08-14)

The portable `BitMapScale` path now declines a standard planar source whose
declared depth includes a null plane link. Null planes are a special source
form for `BltBitMap`, not an implicit zero-plane contract for scaling. The
guard runs before source sampling or destination/extent publication; direct
and register regressions preserve the original extents, destination bytes,
D0, and cycles for native/provider fallback. RTG/CyberGraphX and private
bitmap ownership remain separate.

## G03/G04 TextFit dual-constraint ownership (2026-08-14, superseded 2026-08-18)

This historical dual-constraint interpretation was superseded on 2026-08-18
after checking the Kickstart/AROS-compatible contract: an explicit
`TextExtent` is the complete constraint, and D2/D3 are used only when A3 is
NULL. See the current `G03/G04 TextFit alternate-constraint selection` entry
below.

## G12 WaitBlit queued-work boundary (2026-08-14)

`WaitBlit` now waits only for a hardware blit already in flight. Nodes still
waiting in the `QBlit`/`QBSBlit` scheduler queues remain pending and are not
drained by the synchronous wait, matching the Kickstart contract. Direct FIFO,
timed register-adapter, scheduler, and native-ROM-overlay regressions verify
the unchanged cycle/D0 result and that queued nodes remain available for the
later scheduler boundary ([WaitBlit autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html)).
Hardware busy completion, callback cleanup, queue fairness, exact Agnus
timing, and provider/native ownership remain separate gates.

## G12 V39+ single-FIFO queue ordering (2026-08-14)

The scheduler now keeps `QBlit` and `QBSBlit` requests in one submission FIFO,
as Kickstart V39+ documents. A beam-synchronized head gates later ordinary
requests; a ready QBS node no longer jumps ahead of an earlier QBlit node.
Direct FIFO, scheduler, and mapped native-overlay coverage preserve signed
beam metadata, strict submission order, D0/cycles, and later callback
dispatch ([QBSBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/QBSBlit)).
Exact Agnus beam wake timing and provider/native queue ownership remain open.

## G17 native ActiView readability boundary (2026-08-14)

The host screen/view bridge now distinguishes the compact compatibility image
from an explicitly discovered native graphics.library base when deciding
whether a repeated `LoadView(NULL)` is already satisfied. An unmapped
`GfxBase->ActiView` field on the compact host image retains its historical
host-cache idempotence, while the same unreadable field on an even native base
is treated as unknown provider/native state and the blank handoff remains
visible. The focused AmigaBoot regression exercises the native-base path and
preserves the queued frame-boundary publication; odd bases remain rejected by
the existing native alignment gate. Exact ROM fault timing and provider-owned
display publication remain separate gates.

## G15/G18 LoadView(NULL) DMA-preservation closeout (2026-08-14)

The synthetic frame-boundary handoff now changes only the copper pointer for a
NULL View and leaves the existing DMACON enable state untouched. This preserves
sprite DMA after `LoadView(NULL)` and avoids re-enabling bitplane DMA that a
native/provider owner intentionally disabled. A PAL AmigaBoot regression checks
the DMA mask before and after the queued blanking boundary. The contract follows
the Kickstart LoadView note that sprites continue unless `OFF_SPRITE` is issued
([LoadView autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/LoadView)). Exact
custom-chip DMA timing, provider display ownership, and native CopperSharp68k
execution remain separate gates.

## G14/G18 OpenScreen palette rollback (2026-08-14)

Tagged `OpenScreenTagList` color payloads now use a request-scoped palette
transaction. `SA_Colors` and `SA_Colors32` updates are staged before the
synthetic Screen envelope exists, then committed only after screen allocation,
`VideoControl`, and display reconstruction succeed. Any allocation, provider,
or `RethinkDisplay` failure restores the prior palette and loaded flag before
the next screen request. A PAL boot regression exhausts fast memory after a
`SA_Colors32` request, verifies the documented no-memory result, and confirms
that the next untagged screen publishes the standard synthetic default color.
CyberGraphX palette ownership and exact resident-ROM failure timing remain
separate gates.

The rollback gate also covers a semantically unsupported `SA_VideoControl`
tag after a valid `SA_Colors32` update. The failed open leaves the caller's
`SA_ErrorCode` untouched, restores the prior palette, and allows the next
untagged standard screen to publish the reset-scoped default color. This
keeps malformed and provider-owned VideoControl handling from leaking a
partially staged palette into a later synthetic session.

## G15/G18 display-database QueryHeader length closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `GetDisplayInfoData` builder now publishes
`QueryHeader.Length` as the local payload size in double-longwords, excluding
the 16-byte `QueryHeader`, matching the public `graphics/displayinfo.h`
contract. Direct and mapped native-overlay coverage verifies the corrected
lengths for `DTAG_DISP`, `DTAG_DIMS`, `DTAG_MNTR`, and `DTAG_NAME`; chunk sizes,
payload fields, and the CyberGraphX/provider boundary are unchanged.

## G03/G04 SetFont RastPort-state closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `SetFont` path now matches the classic RastPort ownership
boundary: it selects the guest `TextFont` and refreshes only `TxWidth`,
`TxHeight`, and `TxBaseline`. Caller-owned `AlgoStyle` and `TxSpacing` bytes
survive the switch, including a late cache-write rollback. Direct-core and

the void D0/cycle contract. Broader font/provider failure parity, exact ROM
timing, and CyberGraphX remain separate gates.

## G20 sprite-image display-DMA admission closeout (2026-08-14)

`AllocSpriteDataA` now treats the generated `ExtSprite` image stream as a
custom-chip display-DMA resource when the active memory adapter exposes
`IGraphicsDisplayMemory`. The complete image span—including its eight-byte
position/control prefix and every converted row—is checked before the image
is cleared or published. The public `ExtSprite` envelope remains a public
allocation, and a failed DMA admission releases both owned spans. Direct
regressions cover exact-span acceptance, non-DMA rejection, and cleanup;
CyberGraphX/software-sprite providers, scheduler ownership, and exact native
sprite-fetch timing remain separate gates.

## G20 simple-sprite ChangeSprite display-DMA admission closeout (2026-08-14)

`ChangeSprite` now applies the same optional display-memory admission to a
caller-provided simple-sprite image that `AllocSpriteDataA` applies to a
generated image. The sidecar receives the complete eight-byte POS/CTL prefix
plus all rows before the guest image pointer is published; a rejected range
leaves the pointer, backend callback, and register frame untouched. Plain
`IGraphicsMemory` layouts remain permissive when no address-class predicate is
available. Direct and CopperStart-register coverage exercises rejection,
exact-span acceptance, and the transparent native/provider decline contract.

## G20 extended-sprite ChangeExtSpriteA display-DMA admission closeout (2026-08-14)

The standard hardware form of `ChangeExtSpriteA` now applies the same
display-DMA admission to the source `PosCtlData` image span, including the
word-width expansion for wide sprites. A rejected source leaves the old public
envelope untouched; a native-overlay register decline preserves D0, cycles,
and the program counter for the resident/provider owner. Software-sprite and
scan-doubled tag forms continue through their explicit provider boundary.

## G07 ClearEOL/ClearScreen guest-font geometry closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable clear vectors now prefer the selected guest `TextFont.tf_YSize`
for the text-line height, while retaining the `RastPort.TxBaseline` origin
and the host-only cached `TxHeight` fallback used by synthetic font backends
that have no readable guest font envelope. Direct core, register, and mapped
CopperStart coverage proves a stale cached height cannot shorten a clear.

## G07 ClearEOL/ClearScreen combined-mode BPen closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable clear vectors now follow the native `bgfill_pen()` rule by
testing the JAM2 bit itself, then route the temporary clear pen through the
existing `RectFill` minterm path. `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` therefore toggles the
selected BPen source and `JAM2|INVERSVID` writes the inverse-source BPen,
while pure `COMPLEMENT` and `INVERSVID` continue to use pen zero. Direct and
mapped CopperStart regressions cover the combined-mode results and preserve
the void D0/cycle contract. Layer damage, exact resident-ROM timing, and
provider-owned surfaces remain separate gates.

## G08 Flood seed-color field ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `Flood` entry now reads `RastPort.OutlinePen` only for outline
mode (`mode==0`). Seed-color mode (`mode==1`) compares against the seed pixel
and therefore no longer claims a call merely because the unrelated outline
pen byte is unreadable. Temporary-raster, area-pattern, rollback, and
layer-provider ownership remain unchanged.

## G07 RectFill mode-specific BPen ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `RectFill`/`BltPattern` path now reads `RastPort.BgPen` only
when the selected source/draw-mode can consume it. Null-pattern JAM1,
ordinary null-pattern JAM2, and complement-JAM2 fills no longer fail merely
because the unrelated BPen byte is unreadable; inverse-video JAM2 and
non-complement patterned JAM2 retain the required BPen dependency. This keeps
the field boundary aligned with the native no-pattern fast path.

## G04 Text mode-specific BPen ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `Text` path now reads `RastPort.BgPen` only for JAM2 requests,
where source-zero glyph/template cells can consume the background pen.
JAM1, complement, and JAM1|INVERSVID requests therefore remain claimable when
that unrelated byte is unreadable. Direct and mapped CopperStart coverage
proves the glyph write, cursor update, D0, and cycle contract; color-font,
layer/provider, and exact resident-ROM timing remain separate gates.

## G07 BltPattern COMPLEMENT|JAM2 source ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable area-fill path now takes the `COMPLEMENT|JAM2` whole-region
inversion shortcut before reading `AreaPtSz` or dereferencing `AreaPtrn`.
An attached pattern is therefore not allowed to veto a valid inversion through
an odd, unreadable, or provider-owned source envelope. Direct and mapped
CopperStart coverage proves the selected planar region still inverts and the
void D0/cycle contract is preserved; patterned non-complement modes retain
their source validation.

## G08 AreaEnd COMPLEMENT|JAM2 field ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

`AreaEnd` now shares the `BltPattern` admission boundary: a
`COMPLEMENT|JAM2` area fill does not read `BgPen`, `AreaPtSz`, or the attached
area-pattern words because the selected region is inverted as a whole. The
same mode-specific rule remains active for inverse-video JAM2 and real
non-complement patterns that can consume BPen. Direct and mapped CopperStart
coverage proves polygon fill, collector reset, and void ABI behavior.

## G07 BltTemplate COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable template blit now admits `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` without reading
`RastPort.BgPen`. Template zero cells still participate in the inversion, but
the planar pixel writer ignores the supplied colour and toggles each selected
destination plane from its current bit. Direct and mapped CopperStart
coverage proves the complete template result and void D0 contract while
retaining the BPen dependency for non-complement JAM2 templates.

## G04 Text COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The planar `Text` path now admits `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` without reading
`RastPort.BgPen`. That mode inverts the complete template/text envelope, and
the pixel writer ignores the supplied colour; ordinary JAM2 and inverse-video
JAM2 retain their background-pen dependency. Direct and mapped CopperStart
coverage verifies the glyph envelope, cursor, D0, and cycle behavior.

## G08 Flood COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The portable `Flood` path now reads `BgPen` only when a non-complement JAM2
source can consume it: a real area pattern or inverse-video null pattern.
Null-pattern `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` seed fills invert the selected destination
planes without consulting `BgPen` or `AreaPtSz`. Direct and mapped coverage
verifies the connected fill and void register contract.

## G06 Draw/PolyDraw COMPLEMENT|JAM2 BPen ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The line renderer and PolyDraw preflight now read `BgPen` only for
non-complement JAM2 line sources. `JAM2|COMPLEMENT` still toggles both line
pattern phases, but the pixel writer ignores the supplied colour for the
source-zero phase. Direct and mapped Draw coverage verifies the line pattern,
connected state, D0, and cycle contract; PolyDraw uses the same admission
predicate.

## G06 Draw/PolyDraw COMPLEMENT foreground-pen ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The same planar source rule now applies to `FgPen`: `Draw`, `PolyDraw`,

## G20 generic extended-node association closeout (2026-08-14)

`GfxAssociate` now retains the documented opaque pointer-to-node association
for every `GfxNew` node type. `SpecialMonitor` and `MonitorSpec` do not expose
the `ViewExtra`/`ViewPortExtra` backwards-link fields, so their association is
kept in the registry without inventing a guest field. Re-association removes
older opaque aliases, and `GfxFree` purges backlink-free entries before

lookup, reassociation, teardown, D0, and cycle preservation; provider-owned
foreign nodes and CyberGraphX remain outside this portable boundary.

`AddVSprite` now preserves the caller-owned low flag byte while clearing

and `VSOVERFLOW`) as the node is admitted to a new GELS list. The flag

## G21 InitGels sentinel-state closeout (2026-08-14)

`InitGels` now initializes both the current and previous coordinates of the
head/tail sentinels to the signed extrema used by the sorted GELS list, and
links the head sentinel's `ClearPath` to the tail sentinel. This preserves the
Kickstart background-restore/list contract while retaining caller-owned
`GelsInfo` bounds and the transactional rollback envelope. Direct coverage
asserts the sentinel fields; late-publication coverage verifies the expanded
write set restores both guest structures and the boundary vector.

## G22 AddBob/RemIBob flag-domain closeout (2026-08-14)

The Bob lifecycle now keeps the two classic flag domains separate. VSprite
`SAVEBACK`/`BACKSAVED` controls raster background ownership, while Bob
`SAVEBOB`/`BOBISCOMP` remains caller-owned mode state and Bob system bits are
admitted as `BWAITING`, published as `BDRAWN`, and cleared on `RemIBob`.
Admission preserves only the low user byte, establishes the reciprocal Bob ↔
VSprite link, and the background path publishes its status in the VSprite
envelope. Direct and mapped lifecycle coverage now exercises stale-system-bit
cleanup and save/restore behavior without conflating the two structures.

## G23 Compact collision-table admission (2026-08-14)

`DoCollision` now accepts the Kickstart form in which the collision-handler
table is allocated only through the highest callback entry the caller uses.
Admission probes the mandatory first longword (boundary/routine zero), while
higher entries are read only when a selected mask bit requests them. A sparse
guest-memory regression proves that a one-entry table still dispatches a
routine-zero GEL collision; the full-table path remains covered by the existing
mask and boundary test.

The same admission guard now rejects a stale `head.Prev` link before invoking
the collision backend. The head dummy is the only list node whose predecessor
must be NULL; checking it keeps malformed sentinel state unclaimed without
changing valid sorted-list traversal.

## G08 Zero-capacity InitArea buffer closeout (2026-08-14)

`InitArea` now follows the resident descriptor-publication contract for every
capacity. It validates and snapshots only the even, fully addressable
`AreaInfo` envelope plus the checked 32-bit vector/flag arithmetic, then
publishes `VctrTbl`, `VctrPtr`, `FlagTbl`, `FlagPtr`, `Count`, and `MaxCount`
without dereferencing caller-owned vector/flag storage. Positive, zero, odd,
and currently unmapped buffer pointers are therefore descriptor data at this
vector. `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`, and `AreaEnd` retain their
consumer-owned capacity/readability checks, including the empty collector's
no-op close. Direct and mapped coverage proves publication and the strict
consumer decline.

## G08 Zero-capacity InitTmpRas buffer closeout (2026-08-14)

`InitTmpRas` now admits the native empty descriptor form with a NULL buffer
and zero byte count. The initializer only publishes `RasPtr` and `Size`; no
temporary bytes are dereferenced until a later AreaEnd/Flood/Text operation,
so the empty form is safe and keeps the descriptor retryable. Positive-size,
odd, and currently unmapped backing pointers are equally descriptor data at
this vector; those consumers retain the complete operation-specific capacity
and readable-span checks. Direct and mapped CopperStart coverage verifies the
zero-capacity result and void-vector register/cycle behavior. The contract follows the
[`InitTmpRas` implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/inittmpras.c).

## G08 Zero-capacity AreaEnd closeout (2026-08-14)

The empty `InitArea(areaInfo, NULL, 0)` descriptor is now consumable by
`AreaEnd` as the documented no-op. The shared AreaInfo reader accepts the
all-null storage/cursor form only when both `Count` and `MaxCount` are zero;
non-empty or partially-null collectors remain strict. Direct and mapped
CopperStart regressions verify the empty close and void D0 behavior without
requiring a dummy five-byte vector buffer.

## G08 AreaInfo exact-end address closeout (2026-08-14)

`InitArea` now treats the vector/flag storage end as an exclusive guest
address. A valid two-vector buffer whose final flag byte is at `$FFFFFFFF`
is accepted, while an end beyond the 32-bit address space remains rejected.
Sparse high-address direct coverage verifies the published vector and flag
cursor pointers. The fix keeps the CopperSharp68k guest layout and its
consumer-owned readable-span checks.

## G08 InitArea descriptor-only ownership (2026-08-14)

The portable `InitArea` transaction now mirrors AROS/Kickstart's field writes:
it preflights the descriptor and address arithmetic, then atomically publishes
the vector/flag table and count fields without reading the supplied storage.
This keeps sparse or temporarily unmapped caller buffers available to a future
CopperSharp68k/native owner while the area consumers remain responsible for
usable storage. Source: [AROS `InitArea`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initarea.c).

## G19 Zero-width pixel-line ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The Kickstart V36 pixel-line contract permits a non-negative UWORD width,
including an empty line. `ReadPixelLine8` and `WritePixelLine8` now claim
width zero after confirming a non-layered RastPort, without probing bitmap,
mask, pen-array, or temporary-rastport storage that cannot be consumed. The
direct and CopperStart register paths return zero while preserving D0/cycles;
layered, RTG, negative-width, and non-empty calls retain their existing
provider/portable ownership gates. The documented non-negative width rule is
captured by the [graphics autodoc](https://www.theflatnet.de/pub/cbm/amiga/amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node05A6.html).

## G05 SetMaxPen zero-request ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

`SetMaxPen(rp, 0)` now returns before reading `RastPort->Mask`, matching the
Kickstart/AROS implementation's field-free no-op branch. This preserves the
portable/native boundary for NULL, odd, truncated, and provider-owned
RastPorts while retaining strict mask admission for nonzero requests. Direct
and CopperStart mapped coverage verifies zero host reads, D0, and cycle
preservation; the nonzero mask path remains unchanged. The source basis is
the [AROS SetMaxPen implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setmaxpen.c).

## G15 FreeVPortCopLists link-only teardown closeout (2026-08-14)

`FreeVPortCopLists` now snapshots and clears only the four public
`ViewPort` copper links (`DspIns`, `SprIns`, `ClrIns`, and `UCopIns`). The
portable path no longer reads the unrelated `ViewPort` header before a
teardown, matching the native routine's guest-field contract while retaining
all-or-nothing rollback if a later link write fails. Direct and CopperStart
mapped coverage verifies that an unreadable display dimension does not steal a
valid teardown from the native/provider boundary. The source basis is the
[AROS FreeVPortCopLists implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c).

## G01 SetOutlinePen exact-field ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

`SetOutlinePen` now preflights and snapshots only `RastPort->AOlPen` and the
`Flags` word, then publishes the new outline pen and `AREAOUTLINE` bit with
the existing rollback path. Unreadable `DrawMode`, `AreaPtSz`, and
`linpatcnt` bytes no longer make a valid setter fall through to native/provider
ownership. Direct and CopperStart mapped regressions cover the old-pen result,
flag publication, D0, and cycles. The source basis is the
[AROS SetOutlinePen implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setoutlinepen.c).

## G04 SetFont exact-cache ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

`SetFont` now preflights only the font pointer, `AlgoStyle`, and the three
cached metric words it publishes. It leaves caller-owned `TextFlags` and
`TxSpacing` outside the access envelope while retaining the documented soft-
style reset and transactional rollback. Direct and CopperStart mapped tests
verify the selected font, cached metrics, unchanged spacing, D0, and cycles
when the intervening fields are unreadable. The source field contract is
grounded in the [AROS SetFont implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c).

## G05 SetMaxPen write-only nonzero ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

The nonzero `SetMaxPen` path now derives the contiguous mask and writes only
`RastPort->Mask`; it no longer pre-reads the previous mask byte. This matches
the resident routine's field access and keeps a writable-but-unreadable mask
available to the portable owner instead of falsely declining to native/provider
ownership. Direct and mapped read-fault regressions verify the new mask,
unchanged D0/cycles, and the existing zero-request no-op. The source basis is
the [AROS SetMaxPen implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setmaxpen.c).

## G05 RastPort setter minterm-cache ownership closeout (2026-08-14)

`SetAPen`, `SetBPen`, `SetDrMd`, and `SetABPenDrMd` now treat the eight
`RastPort` minterm bytes as a derived private cache: the portable path validates
their guest address and publishes regenerated bytes, but does not require the
old cache to be readable. When a provider faults those reads, rollback state is
reconstructed from the old foreground/background/draw-mode scalar fields. This
matches the native field access shown by the [AROS SetAPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c),
[SetBPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setbpen.c),
[SetDrMd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setdrmd.c),
and [SetABPenDrMd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setabpendrmd.c)
sources. Direct and CopperStart mapped regressions cover all four setters,
derived minterms, line-pattern restart, private no-pens clearing, D0, and
cycle preservation.

## G06 Move exact write-envelope closeout (2026-08-14)

`Move` now validates the guest addresses for `cp_x`, `cp_y`, and `linpatcnt`
without requiring their old bytes to be readable. The native vector only reads
`Flags` to set `FRST_DOT`; the old cursor and pattern phase are rollback data,
not operation inputs. Readable spans still receive exact transactional rollback,
while write-valid/read-faulting cursor state remains claimable by the portable
or future native path. Direct and CopperStart mapped regressions cover both
faulted cursor words and faulted line phase, along with cursor publication,
fresh-line phase, D0, and cycle preservation. The field contract follows the
[AROS Move implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/move.c).

## G06 WritePixel private-colour provider boundary (2026-08-14)

`WritePixel` now treats `RPF_NO_PENS` as an explicit private graphics-context
colour boundary. Native `graphics.library` obtains the colour from a provider
sidecar in that mode; the portable standard-planar path has no such sidecar,
so it declines before reading `FgPen` or mutating bitmap planes. Direct and
CopperStart mapped tests fault `FgPen` while asserting the unchanged planes,
register frame, and cycle count. The source contract follows the
[AROS WritePixel implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/writepixel.c).

## G06 Draw/PolyDraw private-colour provider boundary (2026-08-14)

`Draw` and `PolyDraw` now decline `RPF_NO_PENS` RastPorts before reading the
public `FgPen`/`BgPen` bytes. Native AROS routes these vectors through a
private graphics-context (`RP_FGCOLOR`/`RP_BGCOLOR`), so the portable planar
path must leave the provider-owned colour sidecar available rather than draw
with stale public pens. Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage faults both
public pen bytes and verifies that no destination planes, registers, or cycles
are changed. The field contract follows the [AROS Draw source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c),
[PolyDraw source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c),
and [private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

## G08 DrawEllipse private-colour provider boundary (2026-08-14)

`DrawEllipse` now performs the same opportunistic `RPF_NO_PENS` check before
reading public `FgPen`. Native ellipse rendering receives its colour through
the private graphics context, while a sparse guest without a readable internal
flag remains eligible for the normal public-pen path. Direct and CopperStart
mapped coverage faults `FgPen` and verifies that no ellipse pixels, registers,
or cycles change. The source contract follows the [AROS DrawEllipse source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/drawellipse.c)
and [private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

## G07 RectFill/BltPattern private-colour provider boundary (2026-08-14)

`RectFill` and `BltPattern` now decline a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` flag before
probing public APen/BPen state. Native AROS routes both the solid and patterned
paths through private GC colours; the portable planar implementation therefore
leaves that provider-owned sidecar available. The flag probe is opportunistic
because the resident BltPattern field envelope does not consume `Flags`, so a
sparse guest with no readable optional word retains the normal public-pen path.
Direct and mapped coverage verifies private-pen decline and unchanged planes,
registers, and cycles. Sources: [AROS RectFill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/rectfill.c),
[BltPattern](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bltpattern.c),
and [private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

## G07 Clear/scroll minterm-cache rollback ownership (2026-08-14)

`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, `ScrollRaster`, and `ScrollRasterBF`
now treat the eight-byte RastPort minterm cache as derived rollback state.
When a provider-backed guest faults reads from that private span, the portable
path reconstructs the rollback image from `FgPen`, `BgPen`, and `DrawMode`
instead of rejecting an otherwise writable standard-planar operation. This
matches the resident SetAPen/RectFill/EraseRect sequencing while preserving
transactional restoration of readable guest caches. Direct and CopperStart
mapped read-fault coverage exercises erase and both scroll variants; source
ownership follows [AROS ScrollRaster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollraster.c),
[ScrollRasterBF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/scrollrasterbf.c),
and [SetAPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c).

## G11 BltTemplate private-colour provider boundary (2026-08-14)

`BltTemplate` now performs an opportunistic `RPF_NO_PENS` check after its
resident `DrawMode`/bitmap envelope and before public `FgPen`/`BgPen` reads.
When the readable flag selects provider graphics-context colours, the
portable standard-planar path declines without touching template or plane
storage; an unavailable optional flag retains the native public-pen path.
Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage faults both public pen bytes and
verifies unchanged planes, D0, and cycles. The source contract follows
[AROS BltTemplate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/blttemplate.c)
and [private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

## G04 Text private-colour provider boundary (2026-08-14)

`Text` now declines a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` RastPort before probing public
`FgPen`/`BgPen` or touching the planar destination. This keeps the portable
standard-planar renderer behind the same provider-private colour boundary as
`BltTemplate`, while leaving the native/provider Text renderer free to use its
graphics-context colours. Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage preserve D0,
cycles, and plane bytes on the decline. The source dispatch follows
[AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c)
and [private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

## G15/G16 MrgCop hidden-viewport ownership (2026-08-14)

`MrgCop` now consumes only the public `Modes`/`Next` links of a hidden
`ViewPort`, matching the resident loop's `VP_HIDE` branch. Malformed hidden
`RasInfo`, extended-mode, or display payloads therefore remain available to a
native/provider owner while an all-hidden chain claims the documented
`MCOP_NOP` result. Visible nodes retain the strict one-node/DUALPF validation
before copper publication. Direct, mapped, and AmigaBoot regressions cover
the unchanged D0/cycle and guest-copper state. The source basis is the
[AROS `MrgCop` implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/mrgcop.c).

## G15/G17 LoadView hidden-viewport ownership (2026-08-14)

`LoadView` now validates and fingerprints a linked `VP_HIDE` node using only
its public `Modes` and `Next` fields. Hidden RasInfo, BitMap, and display
payloads are not consumed by the resident display traversal, so malformed or
unmapped hidden storage remains available to a native/provider owner while a
valid copper publication proceeds. The portable core, mapped CopperStart
adapter, and AmigaBoot publication cache share the same hidden-node boundary;
unchanged topology remains idempotent. The field-order basis is the [AROS
display traversal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/graphics_display.c).

Validation: the new direct/mapped and AmigaBoot LoadView regressions pass 2/2;
the focused `MrgCop`/`MakeVPort`/`LoadView`/`FreeVPortCopLists` group passes
87/87; `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests` passes 1060/1060; and the
combined screen/lifecycle gate passes 279/279. Sequential emulator and test
project-reference builds complete with zero warnings and zero errors.

## G15/G18 GetVPModeID ColorMap-first ownership (2026-08-14)

`GetVPModeID` now follows the resident field order when a `ViewPort` already
has an instance-owned `ColorMap`: the portable path reads the map link and
resolves the mode without requiring unrelated viewport geometry or `RasInfo`
bytes. The full assembling-chain validator remains for a null-map viewport,
and foreign maps still remain available to the native/provider path. Direct
and CopperStart register coverage faults the `RasInfo` link while preserving
the native mode result and cycle frame. Source: [AROS `GetVPModeID`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/getvpmodeid.c).

## G08 InitTmpRas descriptor-only ownership (2026-08-14)

`InitTmpRas` validates and snapshots only the even, fully addressable `TmpRas`
descriptor before atomically publishing `RasPtr` and `Size`. The resident
initializer does not dereference the caller-owned backing span, so positive,
zero, odd, and currently unmapped pointer/size pairs remain descriptor data at
this vector. AreaEnd, Flood, and Text retain the consumer-owned capacity and
readability checks when they consume the descriptor. Direct and register
gateway coverage verifies sparse-span publication, the void D0/cycle ABI, and
late-write rollback. Source: [AROS `InitTmpRas`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/inittmpras.c).

## G09 InitBitMap descriptor-only ownership (2026-08-14)

`InitBitMap` now mirrors the resident field sequence: it validates the
portable OCS/ECS depth boundary, snapshots the eight-byte geometry/header
prefix, and atomically publishes `BytesPerRow`, `Rows`, `Flags`, `Depth`, and
padding without reading or clearing caller-owned `Planes[]` links. A sparse or
currently unmapped plane table is therefore descriptor data at this vector;
bitmap readers and display paths retain their own declared-depth and DMA
checks. Source: [AROS `InitBitMap`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initbitmap.c).

## G02 SetFont default-font ownership (2026-08-14)

The portable `SetFont` core now resolves a NULL font through the supplied
font backend's default-font owner before validating metrics and publishing the
RastPort cache. Backends without a default remain unclaimed for native/provider
fallback, while the guest-list and compatibility callback paths retain their
existing register behavior. This follows the resident [AROS `SetFont`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c) field sequence.

## G01/G02 SetRPAttrsA default-font delegation (2026-08-14)

`RPTAG_Font=0` now delegates through the same `SetFont(NULL)` backend boundary
in the pure tag-list path. A supplied mapped default remains an optimization,
but a direct CopperSharp68k-compatible caller no longer needs to know the
host's default-font address. Backends without a default still decline without
publishing partial RastPort state. This follows resident `SetRPAttrsA` calling
`SetFont` for the font tag ([AROS `SetRPAttrsA`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setrpattrsa.c)).

## G01/G02 InitRastPort guest-list default (2026-08-15)

The CopperStart `InitRastPort` register path now prefers the rebound guest
`GfxBase->DefaultFont` list when one is installed, then publishes the same
font pointer and cached height/width/baseline as `SetFont(NULL)`. The
compatibility callback remains the host-shim owner when no guest list is
present; a malformed guest default leaves the void vector unclaimed before
the RastPort is cleared. This follows resident `InitRastPort` selecting
`GfxBase->DefaultFont` through `SetFont` ([AROS `InitRastPort`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initrastport.c)).

## G03/G04 SetFont AlgoStyle ownership correction (2026-08-15)

The portable SetFont transaction now follows the Kickstart field contract:
it publishes the selected `TextFont` pointer, clears `RastPort.AlgoStyle`,
and updates the cached `TxWidth`, `TxHeight`, and `TxBaseline` words.
Caller-owned `TxSpacing` remains untouched. Direct-core,
CopperStart-register, and mapped overlay tests cover the reset state and
late metric-write rollback. The reset rule follows the public
[`SetFont` autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0479.html).

## G01/G02 native-overlay InitRastPort ownership (2026-08-15)

The mapped native-overlay `InitRastPort` path now declines when no rebound
guest `TextFonts`/`DefaultFont` list is installed. It no longer projects the
host compatibility callback's font and cached metrics into a native RastPort;
the resident Kickstart vector retains that call. Host-shim calls continue to
use the compatibility callback, while rebound guest-list calls retain the
guest default path above. Direct and mapped ownership coverage preserves D0,
cycles, and the caller's RastPort bytes on decline.

## G04/G05 soft-style scalar ownership (2026-08-15)

`AskSoftStyle` and `SetSoftStyle` now read only the resident
`TextFont.tf_Style` byte for intrinsic-style selection. They no longer require
the full glyph/metric envelope that `Text` and the metric vectors consume.
This keeps sparse native `TextFont` nodes claimable for style queries while
leaving rendering and font selection strict. The result remains the
complement of the intrinsic byte for `AskSoftStyle`; `SetSoftStyle` updates
only enabled non-intrinsic bits in the byte-sized `RastPort.AlgoStyle` and
returns the combined style. Direct and mapped regression coverage preserves
D0, cycles, and the algorithmic byte on the sparse-font path. The source
contract is [AROS AskSoftStyle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/asksoftstyle.c)
and [AROS SetSoftStyle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c).

## G02/G03 AskFont query ownership (2026-08-15)

`AskFont` now has its own four-field `TextFont` query decoder. It copies
`tf_Message.mn_Node.ln_Name`, `tf_YSize`, `tf_Style`, and `tf_Flags` into the
caller’s complete `TextAttr` envelope without applying the nonzero-strike
admission used by `OpenFont`, `AddFont`, or rendering. A readable zero-height
font therefore remains queryable, while malformed or truncated guest fields
