still decline atomically. Direct and mapped register coverage preserves D0,
cycles, and the copied fields. The field sequence follows [AROS
AskFont](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/askfont.c).

### G03 Metric query ownership (2026-08-15)

`TextLength`, `TextExtent`, `TextFit`, and `FontExtent` now use a separate
metric-query decoder instead of the nonzero-strike admission used by
`Text`/`SetFont` and font lifecycle operations. A readable fixed-cell
`TextFont` with `tf_YSize == 0` or unmapped strike storage can therefore
publish its scalar/table-derived measurements, while rendering still declines
without usable glyph rows. Direct and native-overlay CopperStart coverage
proves the query results, D0, and cycles; the resident field/read distinction
follows [AROS `TextLength`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textlength.c),
[AROS `TextExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c),
and [AROS `FontExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/fontextent.c).

## G15/G17 ViewPort default-layout ownership (2026-08-15)

The `InitVPort` `SpritePriorities=$24` resident default now lives beside the
public `ViewPort` field offsets in `GraphicsLayouts`. Portable `InitVPort` and
the synthetic Screen projection consume that one shared value, keeping the
CopperStart host path and a future CopperSharp68k implementation on the same
Kickstart 3.1 guest layout. Existing direct and mapped initialization parity
coverage now asserts the shared constant rather than duplicating the literal.

## G18 native display-database sidecar initialization (2026-08-15)

The private `GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase` sidecar now explicitly probes and
clears its entire public allocation before writing the header and native mode
records. A recycled or poisoned public span therefore cannot leak stale
records or future extension bytes into the CopperSharp68k-facing envelope;
publication remains behind the existing GfxBase pointer transaction and the
CyberGraphX/RTG database remains provider-owned.

## G15/G18 ColorMap default DisplayInfo handle ownership (2026-08-15)

The portable `ColorMap` path now treats `NormalDisplayInfo` and
`CoerceDisplayInfo` as DisplayInfo handles rather than assuming every handle
is a raw ModeID. The valid default-lores record therefore accepts its private
nonzero compatibility handle and `GetVPModeID` resolves it back to public
ModeID `0`; malformed handles remain unclaimed for the native/provider path.
Direct and CopperStart coverage exercises `VTAG_NORMAL_DISP_SET` followed by
`GetVPModeID`, preserving the guest handle, result, and cycle frame.

## G15/G18 native display-database rebind ownership (2026-08-15)

Rebinding the portable graphics registries to a discovered native GfxBase now
detaches an instance-owned `DisplayInfoDataBase` sidecar from the old base
before moving publication. If the guest pointer cannot be read or cleared,
the rebind is refused and the old ownership remains intact. A successful move
can therefore republish the same private database allocation on the new base
without leaking or leaving two published sidecars; provider/native pointers
remain outside the portable owner.

## G15/G17 CurrentMonitor publication (2026-08-15)

`LoadView` now publishes the native GfxBase `CurrentMonitor` field when the
loaded View has an instance-owned, associated `ViewExtra` with a readable,
word-aligned MonitorSpec pointer. The pointer is committed together with
`ActiView`, restored on a status-aware display decline, and included in the
active-view fingerprint so changing the ViewExtra monitor cannot be hidden by
pointer-only idempotence. Compact host images and foreign/provider ViewExtra
objects remain outside this optional native-tail ownership boundary.

## G15/G17 ViewExtra TopLine publication (2026-08-15)

`LoadView` now publishes the native `GfxBase.TopLine` word from an
instance-owned, associated `ViewExtra.TopLine` when the View selects
`EXTEND_VSTRUCT`. The word is prepared and committed atomically with
`ActiView` and `CurrentMonitor`; status-aware display declines restore all
three sidecars. The TopLine word participates in the active-view fingerprint,
so changing an extended View's vertical start cannot be hidden by pointer-only
idempotence. Compact images and foreign/provider ViewExtra nodes remain
outside this optional native-tail path. The field layout follows the classic
[GfxBase header](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0612.html)
and [graphics/view.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/view.h).

## G15/G17 RethinkDisplay native ViewExtra sidecar refresh (2026-08-15)

The CopperStart Intuition `RethinkDisplay` handoff now refreshes
`GfxBase.CurrentMonitor` and `GfxBase.TopLine` through the same owned,
extended-View sidecar boundary as `LoadView`. The refresh is sidecar-only and
does not re-enter copper publication; compact images, foreign/provider nodes,
RTG views, and CyberGraphX remain unclaimed.

## G15/G17 LoadView(NULL) native ViewExtra sidecar teardown (2026-08-15)

`LoadView(NULL)` now clears `GfxBase.CurrentMonitor` and `GfxBase.TopLine`
only when those optional fields were previously published by this portable
graphics instance. The clear is committed and restored with `ActiView` across
status-aware display handoffs; a native/provider replacement is detected and
left untouched. Rebinding to a different native GfxBase relinquishes the old
sidecar claim, preserving the provider boundary. Direct coverage proves both
accepted blanking and declined blanking, while compact images and
CyberGraphX/RTG remain outside the claim.

## G15/G17 AmigaBoot LoadView native ViewExtra seam (2026-08-15)

The AmigaBoot scheduler-owned `LoadView` path now refreshes or clears the
optional native `CurrentMonitor`/`TopLine` sidecars through a sidecar-only
GraphicsServices seam. Idempotent View reloads repair edited ViewExtra fields
without queueing another copper stream, while blanking relinquishes the fields
without issuing a second display publication. The compact CopperScreen image
remains outside the native-tail claim; full native GfxBase envelopes retain the
shared direct/core ownership boundary.

## G15/G17 native overlay envelope retry (2026-08-15)

An idempotent native graphics-library overlay install now retries the portable
registry rebind when Exec exposes the full `GfxBase` MonitorList envelope after
the ROM gateway table was already installed. The retry publishes the private
display database and makes subsequent `GfxNew`/ViewExtra sidecar operations
follow the discovered native base; the compact image and provider-owned
fields remain unclaimed.

## G26 native-base rebind refusal rollback (2026-08-15)

The overlay boundary now verifies that `GraphicsLibraryCore` actually reached
the requested native base before claiming the rebind or publishing sidecars.
A refusal leaves the overlay transition unclaimed and restores the guest font
list to its previous owner, preserving the native/provider retry path instead
of recording a false native-base claim.

## G15/G26 existing native-node backlink migration (2026-08-15)

Rebinding an already-live graphics instance now migrates the guest
`ExtendedNode.xln_Lib` backlink for every owned `ViewExtra`/`ViewPortExtra`
node and resident `MonitorSpec` before the native base becomes authoritative.
The backlink writes are staged and rolled back on a late guest write refusal;
the old base remains the registry owner in that case. New nodes and monitors
continue to publish the discovered native base directly. This is limited to
instance-owned guest linkage; monitor-list/copper-provider ownership and
CyberGraphX/RTG records remain separate boundaries.

## G15/G26 resident MonitorList cutover (2026-08-15)

When resident `MonitorSpec` nodes were opened before native takeover, the
rebind path now moves an exact instance-owned compatibility list into an empty
native `GfxBase.MonitorList`, preserving each node's `ln_Succ`/`ln_Pred` and
the list sentinels. A compact compatibility image with an unreadable private
list is accepted only when all registry-owned monitor nodes are still
unlinked. A readable non-empty or foreign destination list declines without
mutation, preserving provider ownership; all link and backlink writes roll
back together on a late failure.

## G18 resident monitor-name ownership (2026-08-15)

An unnamed `OpenMonitor(NULL, modeID)` now publishes a canonical registry-owned
`pal.monitor` or `ntsc.monitor` C string through the resident
`MonitorSpec.xln_Name` field. The allocation and string bytes are committed
after the monitor/list transaction, so malformed native lists, late envelope
write failures, and provider refusals retain their original single-allocation
rollback behavior. Caller-supplied named opens continue to publish their
caller pointer unchanged. This keeps the public `MonitorSpec` layout useful
to future CopperSharp68k walkers without claiming private provider records or
CyberGraphX monitor families.

## G04/G06 zero-effective-mask admission (2026-08-15)

Portable `Text` and `Draw` now treat a zero effective `RastPort.Mask`—after
bitmap-depth masking—as a successful cursor/line-state operation with no
destination-plane publication. They no longer require the unrelated public
`FgPen` (or `BgPen` for JAM2) byte in that no-write case, so sparse native
envelopes can remain available to the CopperSharp68k/provider path. Nonzero
mask operations retain the existing pen, clipping, pattern, and rollback
contracts.

## G06/G07 zero-effective-mask BltPattern admission (2026-08-15)

Portable `BltPattern` and its `RectFill` caller now collapse the write mask
against the declared bitmap depth before reading `DrawMode`, `AreaPtrn`, or
public pen bytes. A zero effective mask is a successful bounded no-op, so an
unreadable `FgPen`/`BgPen` or source-pattern field remains available to the
native/provider owner; a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker still declines to that
owner. Nonzero masks retain the existing stencil, pattern,
clipping, and transactional planar-write contract.

## G11 zero-effective-mask BltTemplate ownership (2026-08-15)

Portable `BltTemplate` now honors a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker before its
zero-mask fast path. A private-colour RastPort therefore remains available to
the native/provider renderer even when no destination plane is selected, while
ordinary zero-mask templates still avoid source staging and public pen reads.
The selected-plane template path retains its existing word-aligned source,
clipping, preflight, and rollback contract.

## G06 PolyDraw zero-effective-mask pen ownership (2026-08-15)

`PolyDraw` now applies the bitmap-depth mask before its connected-line
preflight reads the public `FgPen`/`BPen` bytes. A valid zero-effective-mask
point stream therefore consumes and publishes the connected cursor/line phase
without claiming unrelated pen storage; private `RPF_NO_PENS` remains an
explicit native/provider decline. Direct and CopperStart register coverage
prove unchanged planar bytes, D0, cycles, and zero faulted-pen reads. Layer
clipping/damage and CyberGraphX remain separate provider gates.

## G06 WritePixel zero-effective-mask pen ownership (2026-08-15)

`WritePixel` now computes the bitmap-depth effective mask before probing
`FgPen` or the inverse-video/JAM2 `BPen` path. A zero-effective-mask pixel
therefore remains a successful bounded no-op without claiming unrelated public
colour bytes; `RPF_NO_PENS` is still an explicit native/provider decline.
Direct and CopperStart register coverage prove unchanged planar bytes, D0,
cycles, and zero faulted-pen reads.

## G06/G08 zero-effective-mask pen admission for DrawEllipse and AreaEnd (2026-08-15)

`DrawEllipse` and `AreaEnd` now collapse the bitmap-depth mask before probing
their public foreground/background pen fields. Zero-effective-mask ellipse
outlines and recorded area fills retain their bounded successful state/reset
contracts without claiming unrelated colour storage; `RPF_NO_PENS` and layer
provider boundaries remain explicit. Direct and CopperStart register coverage
proves unchanged raster/collector state, D0, cycles, and zero faulted-pen
reads.

## G08 AreaEnd/Flood private-colour provider boundary (2026-08-15)

Portable `AreaEnd` and `Flood` now honor a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker
before consuming `FgPen`, `BPen`, or `OutlinePen`. Private-colour RastPorts
therefore decline to the native/provider renderer with the collector,
destination, D0, and cycles untouched; a missing optional `Flags` word keeps
the sparse public-pen path available. Direct and CopperStart mapped tests
prove zero faulted public-pen reads. Layer damage, RTG, and CyberGraphX
remain separate ownership gates.

## G07/G08 Clear, erase, and scroll private-colour ownership (2026-08-15)

`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, `ScrollRaster`, and
`ScrollRasterBF` now honor a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker before their
public `BPen`/`FgPen` admission path. Private-colour requests remain available
to the native/provider renderer without public-pen reads or planar mutation;
an unavailable optional `Flags` word retains the sparse compatibility path.
Direct and CopperStart mapped fault-injection coverage proves the boundary.

## G15/G18 OpenWindow reconstruction rollback (2026-08-15)

The CopperStart Intuition `OpenWindow` bridge now treats the display rethink as
part of the open transaction. If `RethinkDisplay` declines after the window
claim is created, the bridge closes that claim and returns the documented NULL
result, so an unseen failed window cannot keep `CloseScreen` blocked. Existing
screen ownership remains untouched; native/provider display ownership still
controls the reconstruction boundary.

## G15/G18 OpenWindow screen-admission rollback (2026-08-15)

The CopperStart `OpenWindow` bridge now requires `EnsureScreen` to return a
real guest Screen before it invokes display reconstruction. A NULL screen is
treated as a failed handoff even when an empty-view rethink would otherwise
return success; the newly claimed Window is closed and the public result is
NULL. This keeps window and screen ownership atomic while leaving provider and
CyberGraphX display paths outside the compatibility claim.

## G15/G18 OpenScreen NULL-handoff admission (2026-08-15)

`OpenScreen` and `OpenScreenTagList` now require a non-NULL Screen after their
completion callback succeeds. A permissive host/provider callback can no
longer turn an empty handoff into a successful screen-open finalization or an
unnecessary display rethink. The guard preserves the native/provider boundary
while keeping the CopperSharp68k-facing lifecycle contract atomic.
## G15/G18 OpenWindow post-rethink admission

The screen/view lifecycle boundary must verify that a Window still belongs to
the same real Screen after display reconstruction succeeds.  If the display
owner retires or replaces the Screen during that handoff, release the
just-created Window and return NULL; do not leave a hidden ownership claim
that blocks later CloseScreen teardown.  This remains a lifecycle transaction
in the Intuition bridge and does not claim provider-owned windows or views.
## G15/G18 OpenScreen post-rethink identity admission

The screen-open transaction must retain the exact Screen staged before
display reconstruction.  If `RethinkDisplay` retires or replaces that Screen,
the bridge must close the staged Screen, publish failure through the existing
finalization boundary, and return NULL for both `OpenScreen` and
`OpenScreenTagList`.  Provider-owned display objects remain outside this
compatibility claim.

## G15/G26 native display-database clear ownership

`ReleaseNativeDisplayDatabase` now distinguishes an externally cleared
`GfxBase.DisplayInfoDataBase` APTR from a provider replacement.  Once the
instance-owned sidecar is no longer guest-reachable, reset reclaims its
allocation; a nonzero replacement is relinquished without clearing or
freeing provider-owned memory, and an unreadable field remains retryable.

## G15/G18 NewWindow target/type admission (2026-08-15)

The synthetic Intuition bridge must claim only caller-owned custom windows
that target the active compatibility Screen. A non-null `nw_Screen` for a
foreign Screen, or a `nw_Type` for a public/workbench window, is declined
before the compatibility Window is reused or published. Null-target custom
requests retain the reset-scoped compatibility form, and the final claim
boundary rechecks the target after provider/display handoff.

## G15/G18 NewWindow alignment admission (2026-08-15)

Caller-owned `NewWindow` envelopes must begin on a word boundary. The
synthetic bridge declines odd A0 bases before reading `nw_Screen`/`nw_Type` or
changing `Screen.FirstWindow`; the null compatibility form remains valid.

## G15/G18 ScreenToFront alignment admission (2026-08-15)

`ScreenToFront` must reject a nonzero odd `Screen *` before activation or
legacy `ViewPort` selection. The standard CopperStart path preserves the
caller frame and leaves native/provider ownership available for that 68000
address-error envelope; the null form remains an idempotent no-op.

## G15/G18 OpenScreen structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The generic CopperStart `OpenScreen` and `OpenScreenTagList` vectors reject
odd nonzero `NewScreen *` and `TagItem *` bases before configuration,
completion, display reconstruction, or error finalization. Null optional
structures remain valid compatibility forms, while malformed odd envelopes
stay available to native/provider ownership.

## G15/G18 OpenWindow structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The generic CopperStart `OpenWindow` vector rejects a nonzero odd
`NewWindow *` before configuration, window creation, Screen handoff, or
display reconstruction. Null `NewWindow` remains the reset-scoped
compatibility form; odd envelopes remain available to native/provider
ownership.

## G15/G18 CloseScreen structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The generic CopperStart `CloseScreen` vector rejects a nonzero odd `Screen *`
before synthetic teardown or display blanking. The live caller frame remains
unchanged for the native/provider address-error envelope; null remains the
existing compatibility no-op path.

## G15/G18 CloseWindow structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The generic CopperStart `CloseWindow` vector rejects a nonzero odd `Window *`
before synthetic window teardown. Null remains the compatibility no-op form,
while odd envelopes stay available to native/provider ownership.

## G15/G18 Intuition query/title structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The generic CopperStart `ShowTitle`, `SetWindowTitles`, `GetScreenData`, and
`QueryOverscan` vectors reject odd nonzero `Screen *`, `Window *`, and
`Rectangle *` envelopes before host callbacks. Byte-addressed title strings
and screen-data buffers remain legal, and null optional structures preserve
the compatibility forms.

## G15/G18 ModifyIDCMP/AddGList structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The generic CopperStart `ModifyIDCMP` and `AddGList` vectors reject odd
nonzero `Window *`, `Gadget *`, and `Requester *` structures before input or
gadget-list callbacks. Null optional pointers remain compatible, while odd
envelopes stay available to native/provider ownership.

## G15/G18 ViewPortAddress structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The generic CopperStart `ViewPortAddress` vector rejects a nonzero odd
`Screen *` before host viewport lookup. Null remains the compatibility lookup
form, while malformed odd envelopes remain available to native/provider
ownership.

## G24 layer-ROM structure alignment admission (2026-08-15)

The portable layer-ROM and super-bitmap seams now reject odd `Layer *`
envelopes before entering the compatibility registry or a host callback. The
classic null lock form remains a successful compatibility no-op, while the
register adapter preserves D0/cycles on odd-pointer decline and an injected
Layers gateway remains the owner of its own provider/native envelope.

## G14/G15 palette ViewPort alignment admission (2026-08-15)

Palette vectors that consume a `ViewPort *` must reject a nonzero odd base
before reading its `ColorMap`, taking the graphics palette lock, invoking a
host palette callback, or mutating guest RGB storage. The null/no-ColorMap
compatibility forms remain unchanged; an odd envelope stays available to the
resident/native or provider implementation. Native-overlay admission must
apply the same rule before recognizing an instance-owned `ColorMap`.

## G14 palette semaphore impossible-state admission (2026-08-15)

Portable palette vectors must decline an owned `PaletteExtra` whose public
`SignalSemaphore` reports a nonzero owner with a zero nest count. That state
cannot be produced by Exec's semaphore protocol; repairing it in the host
shim could claim a native/provider envelope while it is being published or
released. Direct and register paths must preserve palette bytes, D0, and
cycles on this decline, leaving recovery to the owning boundary.

## G14 PaletteExtra semaphore-prefix corruption admission (2026-08-15)

Pen-sharing vectors must validate the public `PaletteExtra` semaphore prefix
before claiming its allocation lists. A corrupted `ln_Type` or impossible
owner/nest pair is native/provider-owned state, not a host-side invitation to
reinitialize the sidecar. Direct and mapped `ObtainPen` calls must preserve
the register frame and cycle count while leaving the ColorMap and sidecar
untouched.

## G14 ObtainBestPenA tag-item wrap admission (2026-08-15)

`ObtainBestPenA` must reject a nonzero tag-list base whose eight-byte
`TagItem` envelope crosses the 32-bit guest boundary. A permissive host memory
adapter must not turn a wrapped `$FFFF_FFFE` request into a valid precision
query and pen allocation; direct and mapped boundaries must leave the palette
sidecar and caller frame available to native/provider ownership.

## G15/G17 BestModeIDA guest-boundary tag admission (2026-08-15)

`BestModeIDA` must accept a complete aligned `TagItem` at `$FFFF_FFF8` while
rejecting a cursor such as `$FFFF_FFFE` whose eight-byte envelope crosses the
32-bit guest boundary. Direct and ROM-overlay paths must select the same native
mode for the valid `TAG_END` item, and a malformed request must preserve D0,
cycles, and native/provider ownership.

## G15/G18 default-zero viewport ModeID ownership (2026-08-15)

`DEFAULT_MONITOR_ID` is a valid zero ModeID, so `VideoControl` must distinguish
an active `VTAG_VPMODEID_SET(0)` override from the cleared zero in the public
ColorMap word. The portable boundary now tracks override presence separately,
accepts and returns zero through `GetVPModeID`, rewrites an in-place GET to
`VTAG_VPMODEID_SET(0)`, and restores native-viewport fallback after CLR. Direct
and CopperStart mapped-overlay paths share this rule; invalid and foreign mode
IDs remain declined for resident/provider ownership, and CyberGraphX is not
claimed.

## G15/G18 OpenScreenTagList guest-boundary TagItem admission (2026-08-15)

The screen/view lifecycle bridge must accept the final complete eight-byte
`TagItem` envelope at `$FFFF_FFF8` and reject a cursor such as `$FFFF_FFFE`
that would require bytes beyond the 32-bit guest address space. The guard is
applied before tag decoding or synthetic screen publication, preserving the
native/provider handoff for malformed lists while keeping valid terminal tags
compatible with a future CopperSharp68k implementation.

## G15/G17 BestModeIDA continuation-wrap admission (2026-08-15)

The portable display-database tag walker must reject a non-terminal item at
`$FFFF_FFF8` whose implicit next cursor wraps to zero. `TAG_END` may terminate
at the final complete envelope and `TAG_MORE` may redirect explicitly, but a
normal/ignored/skipped item cannot become a valid mode request through a
wrapped low-memory continuation. Direct and ROM-overlay paths must preserve
the original frame for that native/provider handoff.

## G01/G05 RastPort attribute TagItem boundary admission (2026-08-15)

The V39 `SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA` TagItem walker must accept a complete
aligned item at `$FFFF_FFF8`, including an explicit `TAG_MORE` continuation,
while rejecting ordinary, ignored, or skipped items whose implicit next
cursor wraps to zero. The guard must run before tag application or result
journaling so a permissive host map cannot publish a partial RastPort update;
direct and register paths preserve D0/cycles for the native/provider fallback.

## G02/G03 tagged-font TagItem boundary admission (2026-08-15)

Tagged `WeighTAMatch` and font-extension tag walkers must accept a complete
terminal item at `$FFFF_FFF8`, while rejecting ordinary, ignored, or skipped
items whose implicit continuation wraps to zero. Explicit `TAG_MORE` remains
the only legal high-address redirect. The guard must happen before DPI scoring
or extension cloning, preserving the direct/register result and native/provider
ownership on malformed guest lists.

## G20 extended-sprite TagItem boundary admission (2026-08-15)

`AllocSpriteDataA` must accept a complete terminal item at `$FFFF_FFF8`
while rejecting a non-terminal item whose implicit continuation wraps to zero.
The check must precede sprite-option decoding, bitmap conversion, allocation,
and guest publication, so malformed high-address lists preserve D0/cycles and
remain available to the native/provider owner. CyberGraphX is not claimed by
this unit.

## G08 `NOCROSSFILL` area-filler state boundary (2026-08-15)

The public RastPort `NOCROSSFILL` flag is now represented at its Kickstart
layout value (`$0020`) and is carried explicitly through the portable
`AreaEnd` fill transaction. The standard-planar implementation already builds
and applies one temporary mask per recorded polygon or ellipse, which is the
no-crossover shape boundary; this preserves complement behavior for overlapping
shapes while leaving the caller's flag word intact. A future CopperSharp68k
area-filler body can replace that policy without changing the guest layout or
the host/provider seam. CyberGraphX, RTG, and layered damage remain outside
this unit.

## G14/G15 VideoControl TagItem boundary admission (2026-08-15)

`VideoControl` must accept a complete terminal `TagItem` at `$FFFF_FFF8`
while rejecting a normal, ignored, or skipped item whose implicit continuation
wraps to zero. The guard must run before palette/view state mutation or batch
publication; direct calls and register calls must preserve the malformed
request for native/provider ownership. CyberGraphX remains outside this unit.

## G18 GetDisplayInfoData guest-end output admission (2026-08-15)

`GetDisplayInfoData` must accept a complete byte-addressed output chunk whose
last byte is exactly `$FFFF_FFFF`, including an odd buffer base, while
rejecting a chunk that crosses into address zero. The register gateway must
preserve D0, auxiliary registers, cycles, and the original buffer on the
crossing form so monitor or provider ownership remains available.

## G18 unavailable ECS display-record monitor discovery (2026-08-15)

Native display records remain discoverable even when the active chipset cannot
execute the selected ECS mode. `DTAG_DISP` reports `DI_AVAIL_NO_CHIPS`, while
`DTAG_MNTR` still returns the resident PAL/NTSC monitor timing object. This
keeps mode databases and future CopperSharp68k/native providers able to inspect
the timing envelope without making the portable path claim unsupported display
execution.

## G12 queued bltnode linkage publication (2026-08-15)

The portable V39+ QBlit/QBSBlit FIFO must publish the classic system-owned
`bltnode.n` links without moving that ownership into a provider. A new node is
terminated with `n = 0`; when a pending tail exists, the tail links to the new
node. Capacity and guest-write failures are transactional: the host queue and
all guest link bytes remain unchanged. Duplicate in-flight/pending addresses
are declined rather than creating a self-link. The optional link sidecar is
implemented by the portable FIFO and CopperStart scheduler only; legacy
address-only adapters and CyberGraphX/native providers remain free to claim
their own queue semantics.

## G12 QBS profile-frame catch-up (2026-08-15)

The CopperStart QBS scheduler now treats `bn_beamsync` as the profile-bounded
vertical beam value used by `VBeamPos`. A representable target wakes at its
exact profile line start; a target line that the active PAL/NTSC geometry cannot
produce is released at the next frame boundary after submission, following the
Kickstart catch-up rule instead of spinning forever. The gate uses the
canonical bus frame/line clock and preserves the existing FIFO, callback,
cleanup, and CyberGraphX/provider boundaries ([QBSBlit autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/QBSBlit), [VBeamPos autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/VBeamPos)).

## G05/G26 RastPort unknown zero-data tags (2026-08-15)

`GetRPAttrsA` now ignores unknown/private tags even when their data word is
zero, preserving the forward-compatible tag-list and native/provider handoff
contract. Recognized output tags still reject null destinations (with the
existing `RPTAG_MaxPen` no-op exception), and the behavior is covered at the
portable/core boundary.

## G09 FreeBitMap header-alignment admission (2026-08-15)

`FreeBitMap` now rejects an odd nonzero `BitMap *` before reading the public
WORD/LONG fields or releasing any plane/header allocation. Byte-addressable
host memory no longer turns a native 68000 address-error form into a portable
free; the ownership token and allocator state remain intact for a native or
provider implementation. The null teardown form and standard aligned bitmap
release remain unchanged ([AROS `FreeBitMap`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freebitmap.c)).

## G06/G08 AreaInfo RastPort alignment admission (2026-08-15)

Area collectors now reject an odd nonzero `RastPort *` before reading
`rp_AreaInfo` or publishing a MOVE/DRAW/ELLIPSE vector. This keeps the
word/long AreaInfo stream on the native 68000 address-error/provider boundary
even when a host memory adapter can read byte-addressed fields. Aligned
collectors and the macro-level `AreaCircle` helper remain unchanged, and a
declined register call preserves D0, D1, cycles, and the existing collector.

## G06 classic circle/outline macro helpers (2026-08-15)

The shared standard-planar surface now exposes `DrawCircle` as the equal-radius
`DrawEllipse` macro path and `SetAOlPen` as the compatibility spelling of the
transactional `SetOutlinePen` update. Circle symmetry and non-positive-radius
failure, together with previous outline-pen return and `AREAOUTLINE`
publication, are covered directly. These helpers add no public LVO and leave
layer damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing to their existing owners.

## G06 legacy `GetOPen` compatibility spelling (2026-08-15)

The shared standard-planar RastPort layer now exposes `GetOPen` as the
compatibility spelling of the V39 `GetOutlinePen` read. The helper delegates
to the same checked guest byte and therefore keeps odd/truncated ownership and
native/provider fallback identical without creating another library vector.
Direct and CopperStart coverage verifies the stored outline pen and mapped
result/cycle preservation. CyberGraphX/RTG, layer damage, and custom-chip
timing remain separate owners.

Validation: the focused `GetOPen` direct/mapped regression passes 1/1.

## G14 ObtainBestPenA TAG_SKIP cursor semantics (2026-08-15)

`ObtainBestPenA` now resumes a `TAG_SKIP` chain at the first complete
TagItem after the skipped records. The previous portable walker advanced from
the data LONG, landing four bytes into the first non-skipped item and silently
losing later `OBP_Precision`/`OBP_FailIfBad` state. Direct and CopperStart
register coverage now proves that a skipped tag preserves the following
precision and failure policy without mutating the palette; CyberGraphX and
native palette ownership remain outside this unit.

## G14 ObtainBestPenA null TAG_MORE termination (2026-08-15)

`ObtainBestPenA` now treats `TAG_MORE` with a null continuation as a clean
end-of-list, matching the shared `utility.library` `NextTagItem` walker. A
valid empty suffix therefore remains portable and follows the normal
first-free/shared-pen path; malformed odd, wrapped, or cyclic continuations
still decline before palette mutation and remain available to native/provider
ownership.

## G14 VideoControl TAG_SKIP cursor semantics (2026-08-15)

The `VideoControl` collector and `VTAG_BATCH_ITEMS_ADD` linker now resume
`TAG_SKIP` at the next complete TagItem instead of four bytes into the first
non-skipped record. This keeps deferred palette state changes and guest batch
list publication aligned with the shared utility tag ABI; direct and
CopperStart coverage proves both command application and terminal-link
rewriting, while malformed and provider-owned chains remain fail-closed.

## G20 ExtendedSprite tag-list null continuation (2026-08-15)

`AllocSpriteDataA` and the related extended-sprite option consumers now treat
`TAG_MORE` with a null continuation as a clean end-of-list, matching the
shared `utility.library` tag walker. Direct and CopperStart register coverage
proves that a valid empty suffix reaches the default sprite allocation path;
odd, wrapped, cyclic, and unreadable non-null lists remain fail-closed and
available for native/provider ownership.

## G15/G18 OpenScreenTagList large TAG_SKIP arithmetic (2026-08-15)

The synthetic `OpenScreenTagList` screen/view bridge now accepts any
`TAG_SKIP` item count whose eight-byte displacement remains representable in
the 32-bit guest address space. The previous arbitrary 4095-item ceiling was
removed; checked arithmetic still rejects wrapped, unaligned, unmapped, or
cyclic chains before screen publication. A CopperStart Intuition lifecycle
regression proves that a 4096-item skip reaches and applies a following
`SA_Width` item, then closes the resulting screen normally. Native
CopperSharp68k and CyberGraphX display ownership remain outside this portable
tag-decoder unit.

## G02/G05 large TAG_SKIP cursor arithmetic (2026-08-15)

Font-extension tag cloning, tagged `WeighTAMatch` DPI validation, and
`SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA` now treat `TAG_SKIP` as a count of complete
following TagItems and jump with checked 64-bit multiplication. A valid large
skip no longer burns the bounded ordinary-item budget before reaching the
following tag, while odd, wrapped, cyclic, unmapped, and over-budget chains
remain fail-closed. Direct font lifecycle/metric coverage and a CopperStart
RastPort attribute gateway regression exercise the shared guest ABI; native
font matching, layer damage, and CyberGraphX/provider ownership remain
separate boundaries.

## G05 `RPTAG_MaxPen` exclusive-limit readback (2026-08-15)

`GetRPAttrsA` now reports the exclusive pen limit represented by
`RastPort->Mask`: an empty mask publishes the resident 256-pen sentinel, and
each highest mask bit doubles the returned limit (`0x03` reports `4`, while
`0x05` reports `8`). This matches the resident mask walk while preserving the
existing null-output no-op and the explicit provider boundary for unknown or
private tags.

## G05 `SetMaxPen` range admission (2026-08-15)

The portable `SetMaxPen` boundary accepts the documented pen range `0..255`
and treats `0` as the classic no-op. Values above `255` are declined before
the RastPort mask is read or changed, preserving the malformed request for a
native/provider implementation instead of silently truncating it to `0xFF`.

## G09 AllocRaster UWORD gateway normalization (2026-08-15)

The mapped `AllocRaster` vector now consumes only the low WORD of D0/D1,
matching the classic UWORD width/height ABI. High register residue no longer
causes a valid guest allocation to be declined; the matching `FreeRaster`
low-word path remains aligned with the same ownership record.

## G09 AllocBitMap UWORD gateway normalization (2026-08-15)

Superseded by the 2026-08-30 ULONG dimension unit. The earlier low-word
interpretation was incorrect: the [original AllocBitMap declaration](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/AllocBitMap)
and CopperSharp68k SDK use ULONG width, height, depth and flags. Full dimensions
must reach validation unchanged; unrepresentable high-word requests must not
allocate a smaller bitmap. AllocRaster retains its distinct UWORD contract.

## G19 pixel-array UWORD gateway correction (2026-08-15)

The V36 `ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`, `ReadPixelArray8`, and
`WritePixelArray8` gateways now consume the documented low UWORD fields from
D0-D3. High-bit values remain non-negative coordinates/counts instead of
being sign-extended into negative geometry. The explicit layer-provider
contract uses the same UWORD types, while the portable core widens them to
checked host integers for clipping and staging. V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` keeps
its separate signed-LONG coordinate/stride contract. CyberGraphX/RTG
ownership remains outside this portable path.

## G11 BltPattern signed-WORD byte-count gateway normalization (2026-08-15)

The V10 `BltPattern` vector now narrows its documented signed-WORD `byteCnt`
from D4 at the 68k gateway, then carries that typed value through the mapped
RastPort core and explicit layer-provider boundary. High-word register residue
cannot become a false stride; a non-positive low word remains fail-closed when
an external stencil would otherwise be read. CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remains
outside this portable path.

## G10/G11 UBYTE minterm and mask gateway normalization (2026-08-15)

`BltBitMap`, `ClipBlit`, `BltBitMapRastPort`, and
`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` now normalize their documented UBYTE D6 minterm at
the 68k gateway. `BltBitMap` likewise normalizes its documented UBYTE D7
plane mask. The portable core and explicit layer-provider boundary use the
same byte-width contract, so nonzero upper-register residue cannot alter
the planar truth table or plane selection. CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remains
outside this portable path.

## G03/G04 text-vector WORD/UWORD gateway normalization (2026-08-15)

The classic text vectors now use the documented low-register fields at the
CopperStart gateway and explicit layer-provider boundary: `Text`,
`TextLength`, and `TextExtent` consume a signed WORD count, while `TextFit`
consumes UWORD `strLen`/width/height fields and a signed WORD `strDirection`.
Negative signed counts are rejected before guest-string or font traversal;
unrelated high-word residue cannot enlarge a request or change direction.
The portable metric/rendering core retains widened host counts for bounded
internal arithmetic, and `TextLength` continues to publish its classic
sign-extended WORD result. This preserves the CopperSharp68k guest layout
without claiming CyberGraphX/RTG ownership.

The field widths follow the authoritative [Text](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/Text.html), [TextLength](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextLength.html), [TextExtent](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextExtent.html), and [TextFit](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/TextFit.html) autodocs.

## G02/G14 malformed shared-pen read ownership (2026-08-15)

`ObtainBestPenA` now distinguishes an empty shared list from an unreadable
shared ColorMap entry. A malformed shared color word no longer gets skipped
while the portable path claims a different free pen. The direct helper still
returns the documented `-1` failure value, while CopperStart leaves the
register frame untouched so native Kickstart or a palette provider can own
recovery. Valid empty-list allocation continues through `ObtainPen(-1)` so
pen-list ordering and viewport publication remain centralized. CyberGraphX,
RTG palette ownership, and native Exec semaphore contention remain outside
this unit.

## G06 `SetDrPt` macro guest-layout helper (2026-08-15)

The shared portable RastPort contract now includes the classic
`graphics/gfxmacros.h` `SetDrPt` operation even though it has no public LVO.
The helper publishes `LinePtrn`, sets `FRST_DOT`, and resets `linpatcnt` to
15 in one rollback-capable guest transaction. It is available to host callers
and a future CopperSharp68k body without adding a vector or changing the
CyberGraphX/provider boundary.

## G05 `RPTAG_Font` exact `SetFont` transaction envelope (2026-08-15)

The portable `SetRPAttrsA` snapshot for `RPTAG_Font` now covers exactly the
guest fields consumed and published by `SetFont`: the selected font pointer
and the cached height, width, and baseline words. `TextFlags`, `AlgoStyle`,
and `TxSpacing` remain caller-owned RastPort state and are neither read nor
rewritten by this tag. A fault-injection regression proves that an unrelated
`TxSpacing` read fault does not make a valid font/cache update decline. The
remaining RastPort attribute, layer-damage, and provider-owned boundaries stay
open for subsequent G05 units; CyberGraphX/RTG is not part of this change.

## G07 zero-effective-mask clear-vector ownership (2026-08-15)

`ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` now compute the effective destination mask before
reading public pen bytes or staging bitmap storage. A mask that selects no
declared bitmap plane still resets the line-pattern phase and completes as a
bounded standard-planar no-op, including through the CopperStart mapped
gateway, even when `FgPen` and `BgPen` are unavailable. Nonzero masks retain
the existing JAM2 pen selection, transactional preflight, rollback, and
layer/provider admission. CyberGraphX/RTG, layer damage, and custom-chip
timing remain separate goals.

## G07 zero-effective-mask draw-mode-free clear boundary (2026-08-15)

The zero-effective-mask branch now reads the RastPort mask before the public
`DrawMode`, `FgPen`, or `BgPen` bytes. When no declared bitmap plane is
selected, `ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` can therefore complete their bounded
line-pattern reset even when the entire mode/pen range is unavailable. A
direct and CopperStart mapped fault-injection regression covers both vectors;
nonzero masks retain the existing JAM2/background-pen and transactional
failure behavior. Provider/native ownership, layer damage, CyberGraphX/RTG,
and custom-chip timing remain separate goals.

## G04/G06 private-colour draw-state admission (2026-08-15)

The portable `Draw`, `DrawEllipse`, `PolyDraw`, and `Text` paths now inspect
the RastPort's `RPF_NO_PENS` marker before reading public `DrawMode`, mask,
bitmap, font, text-rendering state, or the caller's `PolyDraw` point stream.
A private-colour RastPort therefore remains available to its native/provider
renderer even when those public bytes are unmapped, while ordinary
standard-planar calls retain their existing transactional drawing behavior.
Direct and CopperStart mapped fault-injection coverage spans the mode and
public-pen range, with `PolyDraw` also faulting its point stream;
CyberGraphX/RTG, layer damage, and custom-chip timing remain separate goals.

## G06/G07 private-colour patterned-fill admission (2026-08-15)

The portable `BltPattern` path now checks a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker
before probing the public `BitMap` and write-mask fields. `RectFill`, which
uses the same patterned-fill body, inherits that provider/native boundary.
Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage faults the bitmap pointer together
with the public pen range and proves that private-colour calls decline with
no host faulted read or planar mutation. Zero-mask and ordinary planar fills
retain their existing semantics; CyberGraphX/RTG, layer damage, and
custom-chip timing remain separate goals.

## G07 `ScrollRasterBF` clipped negative-edge union (2026-08-16)

The BF backfill strips now derive their visible bounds from the clipped source
envelope. A negative horizontal or vertical delta with an off-screen logical
left/top edge therefore fills the visible vacated edge instead of submitting
an entirely off-screen `EraseRect`. The diagonal vertical strip still excludes
the already-filled horizontal edge, so the union remains exactly once under
`COMPLEMENT`. Direct and mapped ROM-overlay coverage verifies the clipped
left/top result and preserves D0/cycles; layer damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and
custom-chip timing remain separate goals.

## G03 `FontExtent` result-envelope admission (2026-08-15)

`FontExtent` now preflights its aligned, complete 12-byte guest `TextExtent`
result before requesting metrics from the font backend. A truncated or odd
destination therefore leaves the vector available to native/provider
ownership without decoding or walking the selected font. CopperStart applies
the same register-boundary ordering and preserves D0/cycles on decline. Valid
font-extent publication and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership are unchanged.

The same result-first admission now covers `TextExtent` and `TextFit`, so all
three metric vectors preserve native/provider ownership when their packed
12-byte result cannot be addressed.

## G08 AreaEnd/Flood private-colour planar-state admission (2026-08-15)

`AreaEnd` and `Flood` now honor a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker before probing
the standard-planar bitmap and write-mask state. `AreaEnd` keeps its empty
collector success path ahead of that check, so an unrecorded area remains a
bounded no-op; a recorded area or flood operation declines before public
destination state when a provider/native owner has claimed the private colour
context. A zero public AreaEnd mask still consumes and resets the collector
without reading the bitmap or public pens. Direct and CopperStart mapped
fault-injection coverage proves the ordering for both vectors. Layer/provider
dispatch, CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing remain separate goals.

## G07/G08 clear, erase, and scroll private-colour planar-state admission (2026-08-15)

`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `ScrollRaster`, and `EraseRect` now honor a
readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker before probing standard-planar bitmap or mask
state. Inverted-geometry no-ops remain ahead of that marker, preserving
their bounded success contract. Direct and CopperStart mapped fault-injection
coverage faults the bitmap pointer and public pen range; provider/layer,
CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing boundaries remain separate.

## G11 BltTemplate private-colour planar-state admission correction (2026-08-15)

`BltTemplate` now admits a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker before probing the
public bitmap or mask, matching the provider/native ownership boundary used by
the other portable raster operations. Direct and CopperStart mapped
fault-injection coverage proves that private-colour calls decline without a
faulted public planar read; ordinary template rendering remains unchanged.
CyberGraphX/RTG, layer damage, and custom-chip timing remain separate.

## G07 SetRast private-colour planar-state admission (2026-08-15)

`SetRast` now honors a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` marker before probing the
public bitmap or write-mask fields. Although the vector receives its pen as
an argument, it still claims the standard-planar destination; private-colour
owners therefore retain those fields for their native/provider renderer.
Direct and CopperStart mapped fault-injection coverage proves the decline
without public bitmap reads or planar mutation. Zero-mask and layered/provider
boundaries remain separate.

## G11 Kickstart 3.1 interleaved masked-blit width compatibility (2026-08-15)

`BltMaskBitMapRastPort` now preserves the documented V39/V40 behavior for an
interleaved source `BitMap`: its temporary mask geometry uses the aggregate
guest `BytesPerRow`, so the source walk exposes eight pixels per aggregate
byte and the external mask uses that same aggregate row stride. The widened
view is local to this standard-planar vector and does not rewrite the guest
header. Non-interleaved blits, layer providers, RTG/CyberGraphX, and
custom-chip timing remain separate goals.

## G05 `DrawBounds` signed-word result envelope (2026-08-15)

`RPTAG_DrawBounds` now checks that the non-layered bitmap's right and bottom
coordinates fit the signed WORD fields of the guest `Rectangle` before
publication. An oversized malformed geometry therefore remains available to
native/provider ownership instead of receiving unchecked wrapped bounds.
Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage preserve D0, cycles, and the original
rectangle bytes; layer clipping, CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing stay
outside this unit.

## G07 `ClearEOL`/`ClearScreen` signed-coordinate admission (2026-08-16)

The nonzero-mask clear vectors now reject bitmap right/bottom endpoints that
cannot fit the signed WORD coordinates consumed by their `RectFill` body.
This keeps oversized malformed geometry available to native/provider
ownership before public pens, line-pattern state, or plane storage are
mutated. The zero-effective-mask bounded no-op remains intact, and direct plus
CopperStart mapped tests preserve line-pattern phase, D0, and cycles on
decline. Layer clipping/damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing remain
outside this standard-planar slice.

## G07 `ScrollRasterBF` two-dimensional backfill union (2026-08-16)

The portable `ScrollRasterBF` path now excludes the already-cleared horizontal
strip from its vertical `EraseRect` when both scroll deltas are nonzero. This
keeps the vacated region a union rather than applying the backfill twice at
the shared corner, which is observable under `COMPLEMENT` draw mode. Direct
and CopperStart mapped parity coverage verifies the right and bottom strips,
including their corner, are complemented exactly once. Layer damage,
CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing remain provider/native boundaries.

## G07 `ScrollRasterBF` all-quadrant backfill union (2026-08-16)

The `ScrollRasterBF` strip exclusion now handles both horizontal directions
for both top and bottom backfill. A negative `deltaX` starts the second strip
after the left vacated edge, while a positive `deltaX` ends it before the
right edge. Direct and CopperStart mapped `COMPLEMENT` coverage exercises all
four diagonal quadrants and verifies that each vacated edge, including either
shared corner, is toggled exactly once. Layer damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and
custom-chip timing remain separate goals.
## G15/G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` address-wrap admission (2026-08-16)

`FreeVPortCopLists` now checks the complete four-link guest envelope before
reading or clearing any `ViewPort` copper pointer. A high-memory base whose
last link would wrap past `$FFFFFFFF` declines without touching the wrapped
low-memory words or notifying a display owner. Direct and register-gateway
coverage preserves D0/cycles and the public links; ordinary link-only teardown
and provider/native ownership remain unchanged.

## G15/G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` sparse-link rollback envelope (2026-08-16)

Core rollback now snapshots and restores only the four public copper-link
fields, matching the portable teardown's ownership boundary. A viewport whose
link fields fit below `$FFFFFFFF` but whose unrelated full header tail wraps is
declined with its links preserved when no display-resource owner can claim the
handoff. Direct and mapped coverage preserves D0/cycles; ordinary provider
handoff and the null no-op remain unchanged.

## G15/G16 palette viewport inclusive-longword envelope (2026-08-16)

`IsOwnedViewPortColorMap` and the host ColorMap lock now use the inclusive
`vp_ColorMap` longword end (`offset + sizeof(LONG) - 1`). A valid even viewport
whose field ends exactly at `$FFFFFFFF` is therefore still owned by the
portable ColorMap registry and can pass native-overlay palette dispatch.
Direct and mapped coverage preserve the palette value and cycle frame.
## G09/G19 `BitMapScale` inclusive final plane-link envelope (2026-08-16)

`BitMapScale` now accepts a compact standard-planar header whose final
declared `BitMap.Planes[]` longword ends exactly at `$FFFFFFFF`, while still
rejecting a link field that crosses the guest address space. The register
gateway applies the same inclusive `BitScaleArgs` destination-pointer check;
direct and CopperStart coverage produce identical scaled pixels, extents,
D0, and cycles. RTG/CyberGraphX and display-DMA ownership remain outside this
portable bitmap utility unit.

## G04/G06 `DrawEllipse` optional Flags admission (2026-08-16)

`DrawEllipse` uses `RPF_NO_PENS` only as a readable provider/native colour
ownership hint and never mutates `RastPort.Flags`. A missing or faulted
optional Flags word therefore remains compatible with sparse standard-planar
RastPorts; a readable marker still declines before public colour rendering.
Direct and CopperStart mapped coverage verifies matching ellipse pixels, D0,
and cycles. Layer clipping/damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing
remain outside this unit.

## G19 V36 pixel-array temporary RastPort inclusive-longword envelope (2026-08-16)

The V36 pixel-array helpers accept an explicitly supplied temporary `RastPort`
whose `rp_BitMap` longword ends exactly at `$FFFFFFFF`, including the aligned
base `$FFFF_FFF8`. Direct and CopperStart mapped dispatch share the inclusive
guest envelope; malformed crossing bases remain available to native/provider
ownership. CyberGraphX/RTG, layer damage, temporary-plane ownership, and
custom-chip timing remain outside this standard-planar unit.

## G15/G16 palette viewport inclusive-longword validation closure (2026-08-16)

The viewport palette unit is validated through both direct and native-overlay
dispatch. An owned ColorMap at `ViewPort` `$FFFF_FFF8` is accepted because its
four-byte `vp_ColorMap` field ends exactly at `$FFFFFFFF`; the mapped path
preserves the void-vector D0/cycle frame and publishes the same RGB4 entries.
Provider/RTG ownership and display timing remain outside this portable claim.

## G09/G19 `BitMapScale` inclusive final plane-link validation closure (2026-08-16)

The depth-one compact header whose `Planes[0]` longword ends at
`$FFFFFFFF` is accepted through direct and CopperStart paths. The focused
boundary test, the 18-test `BitMapScale` family, and the 1161-test graphics
scaffold pass with matching scaled pixels, extents, D0, and cycles. RTG/
CyberGraphX and display-DMA ownership remain outside this portable unit.

## G15/G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` sparse-link rollback validation closure (2026-08-16)

The viewport teardown family passes 8/8, including the high-address envelope
guard and sparse-link rollback. Declined requests preserve all four public
copper links, D0, and cycles; the valid owner and null no-op paths remain
unchanged and provider-owned resources are not claimed.

## G15/G16 `MakeVPort` transactional copper-link handoff (2026-08-16)

The portable MakeVPort handoff now snapshots all four public copper links
before side effects and restores them when a status-aware copper builder
declines after publishing partial state. A direct and mapped regression with a
mutating failing builder passes, including temporary ViewPortExtra cleanup,
status/D0, and cycle preservation. Hardware copper timing and provider-owned
display publication remain outside this unit.

## G15/G16 `MrgCop` transactional copper-link handoff (2026-08-16)

The portable merge boundary now journals the four public copper links of each
visible `ViewPort` before a status-aware copper provider runs. A provider that
publishes partial links and then declines cannot leave a half-built chain for
`LoadView` or teardown; all visible links are restored while hidden nodes stay
on their native/provider path. Direct and mapped regression coverage passes,
with the MrgCop family at 15/15 and the full graphics scaffold at 1163/1163.
Hardware copper timing, layer damage, and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remain
provider/native boundaries.

## G15/G16 direct `WaitTOF` scheduler ownership (2026-08-16)

`GraphicsLibraryCore.WaitTOF()` now honors the status-aware frame scheduler
boundary before the legacy display callback. A declining status owner leaves
the direct and mapped void calls unclaimed with D0/cycles preserved; an
accepting owner receives cycle zero for the direct compatibility call and the
guest cycle for the mapped call. The focused regression passes 1/1, the
`WaitTOF` family passes 5/5, and the full graphics scaffold passes 1164/1164.
Isolated emulator and test-project builds remain warning/error free; native
frame timing and provider ownership remain outside the portable implementation.

## G19 V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` signed-LONG register geometry (2026-08-16)

The mapped V40 chunky-pixel gateway now preserves the full signed-`LONG`
rectangle required by Kickstart instead of narrowing D0-D3 to signed WORDs.
Direct and CopperStart coverage writes a row at x=32768 and verifies the
published planar byte, void-vector D0, and cycles; the three-test chunky family,
23-test pixel-array family, and full graphics scaffold pass 1165/1165. The
portable source/stride envelope and layered/RTG provider ownership remain
unchanged.

## Graphics gate audit (2026-08-16)

test project retains its unrelated chipset/CIA/event-journal/JIT baseline
failures. The remaining layered-raster ledger failure is an RTG fixture: its

cannot consume portable `TxHeight`. That CyberGraphX/layer font-state handoff

CopperSharp68k ownership.

## G18/G26 native-overlay monitor lifecycle parity (2026-08-17)

The native-base overlay now has an independent direct-vs-mapped proof for
`OpenMonitor`/`CloseMonitor`. Both paths publish a resident PAL `MonitorSpec`,
reuse it on a second open, decrement the guest `ms_OpenCount` through one and
zero, retain the native `MonitorList` link, and preserve D0/cycles. The mapped
native envelope may own a separate private `DisplayInfoDataBase` sidecar, so
monitor-spec addresses are compared per instance rather than treated as a
shared host allocation. This keeps monitor-list and display-database ownership
separate while preserving the CopperSharp68k guest layout.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayAndHostGatewayPreserveMonitorLifecycleParityAgainstFullNativeEnvelope`.
## G18/G25 native-overlay `CloseMonitor` ownership admission (2026-08-17)

The mapped native overlay now checks that a non-null `CloseMonitor` target is
an instance-owned resident `MonitorSpec` and that its guest `ms_OpenCount`
WORD is writable before entering the portable registry. Null remains the
documented no-op. A read-only provider/native monitor therefore tail-chains
with D0, cycles, and the open count unchanged.

Evidence: `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyOwnedMonitorBeforeClosePublication`.

untouched bitmap endpoint. Writes normalize the mask to the declared bitmap
depth before deciding whether a destination probe is needed, while reads do
not use the write mask to suppress source validation. Direct CopperSharp68k
calls, mapped register calls, and the native overlay now make the same
ownership decision; CyberGraphX and RTG/layer providers remain separate.

### G03/G26 native guarded fixed-cell `TextFit` reverse direction (2026-08-20)

The native `TextFit` overlay now admits the bounded fixed-cell alternate-box
form with `strDirection=-1`. It uses the same positive fixed-cell movement,
height, baseline, and no-style checks as the forward arm and publishes the
same origin-relative envelope. The direction marker is checked only after the
proportional flag is tested; the separate one-declared-glyph negative-cell
arm now claims the narrow proportional reverse form, while richer reverse
requests remain unclaimed for the portable/provider owner.

### G03/G26 native guarded proportional `TextFit` bounded forward walk (2026-08-20)

The native proportional `TextFit` implementation now supports bounded forward
walks of two through eight glyphs. It validates the source/result/font and all
table spans, including the proportional default slot, before selecting each
cell. Every `CharSpace + CharKern + TxSpacing` movement must be strictly
positive. Accepted cells are accumulated into the published `TextExtent`
envelope; if the width box is exhausted, the result is an empty fit.

Reverse paths, style or explicit-constraint forms, zero/negative/reverse
movement, malformed or wrapping storage, provider/RTG ownership, CyberGraphX,
and exact CopperSharp68k timing decline transparently to their existing owner.
The guest body remains CopperSharp68k-compatible while the portable host path
retains the boundary checks.

## G24 layered raster ClipRect/backing-store boundary (2026-08-28)

Validated layered raster execution now has an explicit regression proof that
painting a Super layer with an obscured public partition writes only its
published display, saved-ClipRect, and SuperBitMap fragments. `ReadPixel` and
`WritePixel` also use that same supplied projection to observe and update the
obscured backing value. None of these operations alters Layer flags, the
`DamageList` pointer, or the damage header. Damage and refresh remain a Layers
topology/`BeginUpdate`/`EndUpdate` responsibility; they are not a
graphics.library dirty-region mechanism. The test also keeps the supplied
ClipRect heads authoritative, so graphics.library does not rediscover or copy
Layer topology. CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remains unchanged.

Validation: `ValidatedSuperProjectionCoversPublicBackingAndWholeCallerDomainAtomically`
and the focused layered raster/update filter pass (3/3).

### G06 native scalar `ReadPixel` admission

Status: pass for the bounded standard-planar native form (2026-08-28).

The native reader now claims only a complete, unlayered one-to-eight-plane
BitMap and an in-bounds WORD coordinate. It combines every declared plane with
MSB-first tests, preserves both input coordinates when handing a form back to
the portable/provider owner, and leaves layer clipping, RTG, CyberGraphX, and
out-of-raster `-1` results outside the native claim.

### G06 native scalar `WritePixel` admission

Status: pass for the bounded standard-planar native form (2026-08-28).

The native writer now routes depths one through eight through one transactional
planar body. It validates the full RastPort and BitMap envelopes, rejects the
provider-sidecar `RPF_NO_PENS` form, validates signed-positive stride/rows,
WORD-coordinate bounds, and every selected plane before its first bit change.
Equality at either raster bound declines. Every decline restores D0 and D1 for
the existing portable/provider owner; layers, clipping, RTG, and CyberGraphX
remain outside the native claim.

Validation: depth-two AccurateM68000 MSB-first/high-word success, equality
boundaries, layered fallback, and malformed-selected-plane atomicity pass;
the lifecycle/layer/scalar raster slice passes (41/41). Source-linked image:
2,504,800 bytes / 124,033 branches / 3,778 relays / 7 chains / 3,364 fragment
boundaries.

The scalar regression also covers inverse-video JAM2/BPen publication,
COMPLEMENT toggling, and inverse-video JAM1 plus inverse-video COMPLEMENT
no-op behavior on the same validated depth-two bitmap.

### G06 native `SetRast` planar admission

Status: pass for the bounded standard-planar native form (2026-08-28).

The native whole-raster initializer now validates its complete RastPort and
BitMap envelopes before filling: it rejects layers, `RPF_NO_PENS`, nonstandard
BitMap flags, nonpositive/odd stride, nonpositive rows, and malformed selected
plane links. Selected plane endpoints are preflighted before the first byte is
written. A decline restores the original D0 pen for the portable/provider
owner; layer clipping, RTG, and CyberGraphX remain outside the native claim.

RastPorts return untouched D0/D1 to the portable/provider path.

### G06 native RastPort mask controls

Status: pass for `SetWriteMask` and `SetMaxPen` (2026-08-28).

`SetWriteMask` now claims only the aligned, non-wrapping public `Mask` byte;
it neither consumes pen state nor inspects layer, bitmap, or damage ownership.
`SetMaxPen(0)` remains field-free. Its nonzero arm admits only values through
255, derives the contiguous low-bit mask, and writes that same byte after
pointer validation. Every nonzero decline restores the complete caller D0
before taking the portable/provider fallback, including out-of-range values.
